FClCY3xuSm.one_liner: A linear operator whose kernel captures all independent directions enables GIN testing and TIN rank estimation for latent-variable causal discovery
FClCY3xuSm.problem: Existing GIN and TIN implementations do not fully exploit the statistical structure of linear non-Gaussian models, which may compromise the reliability of causal identification under latent confounders.
FClCY3xuSm.method: Building on the characterization of independence through constant conditional means and variances, the paper constructs a fixed linear operator whose kernel exactly characterizes all independent directions, using only low-order information. It adds a paired-bootstrap GIN test with pointwise asymptotic Type I error control and a jointly calibrated TIN rank estimator.
FClCY3xuSm.key_idea: Characterize independence via constant conditional means and variances, then take the kernel of one fixed linear operator to recover the entire independent subspace without searching projections.
FClCY3xuSm.evidence: Identification results under finite-feature assumptions, pointwise asymptotic Type I error control for the test, and synthetic and real-world experiments with ablations against baselines such as HSIC and LiNGIC.
FClCY3xuSm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the exact linear-operator characterization of the whole independent subspace clean and useful, with a testing procedure that accounts for projection-estimation error.
FClCY3xuSm.main_concern: The baselines may exaggerate the gains because HSIC and LiNGIC use a single direction while the method uses the full null space, and ablations do not show the source of the improvement.

EpLvdiy8ZB.one_liner: Filtering mechanism with total-variation guarantee O~(1/N_B + 1/N_S) to the high-quality distribution, plus nearly matching information-theoretic lower bounds.
EpLvdiy8ZB.problem: Empirical data-filtering heuristics for LLM training lack guarantees on how well the filtered data aligns with the target task.
EpLvdiy8ZB.method: Given N_S high-quality and N_B lower-quality examples, designs a filter that finds more high-quality examples through a constrained problem that keeps margin violations on the positive sample small while minimizing acceptance of the mixture.
EpLvdiy8ZB.key_idea: Solve a constrained linear-separator problem that accepts nearly all target samples while minimizing acceptance on the mixture, giving dimension-free total-variation bounds under a margin assumption.
EpLvdiy8ZB.evidence: Upper and lower bound proofs, an analyzed unknown-margin procedure, and experiments with synthetic Gaussians and Wikipedia versus C4 text using weighted linear SVM and logistic regression.
EpLvdiy8ZB.claimed_gains: Output distribution within O~(1/N_B + 1/N_S) total variation distance of the high-quality distribution, with nearly matching information-theoretic lower bounds.
EpLvdiy8ZB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is clearly defined and the lower bound matches the upper-bound rate, with a careful analysis that also covers the unknown-margin case.
EpLvdiy8ZB.main_concern: The experiments do not test the analyzed method (they use SVM or logistic regression surrogates in regimes with vacuous bounds), and the single-hyperplane margin assumption may not hold for quality-within-topic filtering.

ITXqY4fCHu.one_liner: PreAct rebuilds WebPRM explanations with one generator, pre-execution information only, and no preference labels; WebContrast tests explanation use.
ITXqY4fCHu.problem: When training labels influence how explanations are generated, WebPRMs may learn to recognize labels instead of judging actions.
ITXqY4fCHu.method: PreAct reconstructs both candidates' explanations in WebPRM Collection using one generator and only pre-execution information, without access to preference labels. WebContrast, a benchmark of 300 pages across 119 websites, tests responses to goal changes and stability across explanation versions.
ITXqY4fCHu.key_idea: Generate both candidate actions' explanations with the same generator from pre-execution information only, so explanation style cannot leak preference labels.
ITXqY4fCHu.evidence: Training and evaluation of Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on WebContrast, WebLINX, WebShop, and the WebPRM Collection, with controls for length, paraphrase, generator, and neutral text.
ITXqY4fCHu.claimed_gains: On WebContrast, the effect of the same test explanations shifts from -3.58 to +5.58 percentage points for Qwen3-8B and from -24.25 to +5.33 for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct after PreAct training.
ITXqY4fCHu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that label leakage through explanation construction is a real problem, shown with controlled source-label assignments, and that the evaluation separates goal accuracy, explanation benefit, and stability.
ITXqY4fCHu.main_concern: PreAct changes information access, generator choice, and factual review together so the gains cannot be attributed to a single component, and results are at small scale (1,024 states, verdict-only LoRA SFT).

HDFKzKI82d.one_liner: Training-free speculative decoding drafting from a hierarchical memory of the target model's own predictions, queried most-specific first.
HDFKzKI82d.problem: Training-free drafters either copy text from the prompt, history, or an external corpus, or index the target model's own predictions by a single token, so they use one key granularity and one evidence lifetime.
HDFKzKI82d.method: SuffixSpec casts drafting as retrieval from a memory of the target model's predictions, with suffix-local, token-local, and token-global layers queried in decreasing specificity. A prefill bootstrap populates it before decoding, a dual-timescale commit updates the persistent layer once per request using decode-time predictions only, and a budgeted tree construction spends verification nodes on the continuations the memory scores highest.
HDFKzKI82d.key_idea: Key stored target-model predictions at several context granularities and lifetimes, and query them from most to least specific to build the draft tree.
HDFKzKI82d.evidence: Seven tasks and three models from 8B to 32B parameters, plus in-engine comparisons inside SGLang on Qwen3-8B at 2K- and 8K-token inputs.
HDFKzKI82d.claimed_gains: Up to 2.37x speedup over autoregressive decoding and up to 17.9% faster than the strongest training-free baseline; inside SGLang on Qwen3-8B it reaches 2.26x and 2.51x on 2K- and 8K-token inputs.
HDFKzKI82d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the measurement-driven design well justified, cheap in overhead, and consistently faster than the strongest training-free baselines across models and tasks.
HDFKzKI82d.main_concern: Reviewers cite an unsupported absolute novelty claim (prior work caches prefill predictions), omitted recent baselines, and baselines run in HuggingFace at batch one rather than in a serving engine.

CZ0WxNn3Ex.one_liner: Distills execution-verified teacher repairs of a variable-length diffusion LM's own failures into edit-location prediction and local reconstruction.
CZ0WxNn3Ex.problem: In variable-length diffusion LMs a repair differs in length from the failure it fixes, so masked SFT at fixed positions can only treat the repair as a new response and cannot express which tokens to keep or change.
CZ0WxNn3Ex.method: VEDI obtains execution-verified teacher repairs of the model's own failures, aligns each failure with its repair accounting for insertions and deletions, and jointly trains one backbone to predict where to edit and to reconstruct only the edited region given the preserved context. Inference uses the original sampler without a teacher or repair stage.
CZ0WxNn3Ex.key_idea: Align each failure with its verified repair under insertions and deletions, then supervise edit locations and reconstruct only the edited region given the preserved context.
CZ0WxNn3Ex.evidence: FlexMDM (8B) and DreamOn (7B) on five benchmarks including HumanEval+ and MBPP+, with full-rewrite SFT trained on the same failures and repairs and controlled comparisons.
CZ0WxNn3Ex.claimed_gains: Improves over Base on all five benchmarks with gains of up to 12.7 HumanEval+ points on DreamOn, and exceeds full-rewrite SFT by 6.3 and 5.0 HumanEval+ points on FlexMDM and DreamOn while matching or exceeding it on MBPP+.
CZ0WxNn3Ex.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the failure-specific edit supervision coherent and well controlled, with gains on both backbones and ordinary inference without a teacher or repair stage.
CZ0WxNn3Ex.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate whether variable-length modeling is needed (no fixed-canvas control), the mechanism linking edit training to full generation is unclear, and novelty is seen as incremental.

KIbAm4m9qh.one_liner: RGSM-GP keeps an evolving semantic memory across graph-purification rounds, updated by node-reliability estimates, to improve robustness against structural attacks.
KIbAm4m9qh.problem: Iterative graph purification reuses the same node-feature conditioning every round, so it cannot use the semantic evidence exposed by progressively repaired neighborhoods.
KIbAm4m9qh.method: RGSM-GP estimates classifier-free node reliability from structural correction residuals, edge-posterior uncertainty, and temporal instability across rounds. A budget-normalized soft gate limits memory updates to unreliable nodes, reliability-weighted neighborhoods supply replacement context, and raw features stay fixed anchors for training and final prediction.
KIbAm4m9qh.key_idea: Maintain a semantic memory across rounds, updating only nodes that purifier-derived reliability marks unreliable via a soft gate, with raw features as fixed anchors.
KIbAm4m9qh.evidence: Multi-seed evaluation on Cora, Citeseer, and PubMed under PRBCD/LRBCD attacks against GPR-GAE, AT-GCN, RUNG, and GNNGuard.
KIbAm4m9qh.claimed_gains: Highest robust-average point estimate in six of six PRBCD/LRBCD settings, first at the 50% perturbation budget in five settings, and all six completed robust-average differences favor RGSM-GP, including a 5.94 percentage-point improvement on Cora.
KIbAm4m9qh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear, the design a reasonable response to neighborhoods changing during purification, and reliability estimation without clean-graph or classifier supervision a strength.
KIbAm4m9qh.main_concern: Generality and cost are unverified: only one underlying purification model is evaluated, compute and memory overhead is not quantified, and the semantic memory may collapse to an identity mapping that merely preserves raw features.

ULMDEqp1vD.one_liner: Randomized exact recovery of k-sparse Fourier functions over the Boolean hypercube using O(nk) queries and O(nk log k) time.
ULMDEqp1vD.problem: Existing near-optimal algorithms for exact Fourier-sparse recovery over the hypercube sit within polylogarithmic factors of the Omega(nk) lower bound but rely on sophisticated machinery that makes recovery opaque.
ULMDEqp1vD.method: A randomized algorithm, simpler in design than prior work, identifies all nonzero Fourier coefficients exactly given oracle access to a function whose spectrum has at most k nonzero coefficients. The visible abstract does not describe the recovery mechanism in detail.
ULMDEqp1vD.key_idea: A simpler randomized recovery procedure that attains O(nk) queries and O(nk log k) time; the specific mechanism is not described in the abstract.
ULMDEqp1vD.evidence: Theoretical query and running-time analysis against the known Omega(nk) lower bound; no experiments are stated.
ULMDEqp1vD.claimed_gains: O(nk) queries and O(nk log k) time, sample-optimal up to constant factors with running time within an O(log k) factor of the lower bound, a polylogarithmic improvement over the best known results.
ULMDEqp1vD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the algorithm and analysis are simpler and more accessible than prior work while improving query and runtime complexity, with rigorous proofs.
ULMDEqp1vD.main_concern: Motivation and applicability are limited because the model assumes noiseless, exactly sparse functions, whereas cited applications need noise tolerance or approximate sparsity.

MOIKCu9eSG.one_liner: Empirical study: depth-grown and looped transformers acquire in-context learning earlier and rely more on induction heads than dense models.
MOIKCu9eSG.problem: Looped and depth-grown models reuse computation across depth and show suggestive signs of better in-context learning, but how this reuse shapes the acquisition, retention, and mechanisms of ICL is unclear.
MOIKCu9eSG.method: Compares grown and looped models with a full-depth dense reference on pretrained language models and controlled tasks, traces attention heads through training, and ablates induction-ranked heads.
MOIKCu9eSG.key_idea: Soft parameter reuse across depth, by growing or looping, gives a shared inductive bias toward learning from context and propagates early induction heads across layers.
MOIKCu9eSG.evidence: Pretrained language models up to 3B parameters and controlled tasks (including an Omniglot task separating in-context from in-weights learning), with head tracing during training and induction-head ablations.
MOIKCu9eSG.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports qualitative findings only, such as earlier ICL acquisition and stronger ICL retention than a dense reference.
MOIKCu9eSG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that multiple complementary analyses show grown and looped models are more competent at ICL and acquire it earlier than dense models, with clear writing.
MOIKCu9eSG.main_concern: The finding is seen as unsurprising relative to prior work on improved ICL in looped and grown models, and induction heads are identified only by prefix-matching score without checking copying behavior.

mWownvQcph.one_liner: Factorizes humanoid control into terrain-invariant intent via forward-backward representations and a perceptive terrain-conditioned policy, plus explicit root instructions.
mWownvQcph.problem: Covering terrain-dependent variation in humanoid behavior with terrain-matched demonstrations requires enumerating a combinatorial space of behaviors and terrain geometries.
mWownvQcph.method: A forward-backward representation maps motion references, target states, and reward functions into a shared intent space without terrain information, while a perceptive policy realizes each intent under the surrounding terrain geometry. Explicit Root Instructions (ERI) separate global transport (heading, planar velocity) from behavioral intent.
mWownvQcph.key_idea: Encode behavioral intent without terrain information, let a perceptive policy realize it under local terrain geometry, and supply root heading and velocity explicitly to preserve global progress.
mWownvQcph.evidence: Adapts flat-ground humanoid motion priors to diverse terrains without terrain-specific demonstrations; reviews cite ERI and perception ablations and real-world experiments (abstract is truncated).
mWownvQcph.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is truncated before any results.
mWownvQcph.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating behavioral intent from terrain-conditioned execution is a clear design that reduces reliance on terrain-matched demonstrations, with real-world demos showing robustness.
mWownvQcph.main_concern: Experimental support is thin: baselines are lacking, ablations do not isolate terrain-agnostic intent encoding in the backward representation, and ERI adds supervision beyond prior unsupervised RL work.

m9YLwQz1CG.one_liner: Small frequency gaps (beats), not long periods, can break RoPE extrapolation; stretching the gaps repairs much of the damage.
m9YLwQz1CG.problem: RoPE degrades beyond its training length, and the common account blames planes whose period exceeds the training window, which cannot explain collapse in spectra where every period is short.
m9YLwQz1CG.method: Treats the rotary logit as a trigonometric polynomial of the offset and applies super-resolution bounds that tie extrapolation error to frequency gaps. It tests this in small character-level models with constructed detuned frequency pairs, using gap-stretching and beat-envelope-capping interventions.
m9YLwQz1CG.key_idea: A frequency gap epsilon with epsilon*L <= 1/2 means training offsets no longer determine the rotary logit stably, raising worst-case error near the half-beat offset by a factor 1/(epsilon*L).
m9YLwQz1CG.evidence: Character-level models with 0.46M and 3.3M parameters, a sweep over eight beat periods, ten times longer training, and a second corpus.
m9YLwQz1CG.claimed_gains: Stretching only the gaps at inference removes 52-86% of the damage where a model has failed, versus at most 9% for an equal shift that keeps them; capping beat envelopes removes all excess at the 2,048-token and slower beats and 31-79% at faster ones.
m9YLwQz1CG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a new, controlled counterexample to period-based explanations of RoPE failure, with causal evidence that the failure point tracks the beat length and a quick gap-based remedy.
m9YLwQz1CG.main_concern: External validity is limited: experiments use tiny character-level models (0.46M and 3.3M parameters), and the gap explanation works on constructed spectra without pretrained-model or retrieval-task evaluation.

Kooe7QMXgS.one_liner: Exact solver for maximum-likelihood ranking from pairwise preferences, fast enough to replace Borda-style heuristics on practical ML instances.
Kooe7QMXgS.problem: Exact maximum-likelihood ranking from pairwise comparisons is NP-hard, so ML pipelines settle for heuristics such as Borda counts, win ratios, and greedy cycle removal that compromise ranking quality.
Kooe7QMXgS.method: XRank is an exact solver that substantially outperforms existing exact methods; the keywords point to integer programming for the linear ordering problem, but the abstract does not detail the mechanism. It is used to re-solve ranking instances from 9 publications.
Kooe7QMXgS.key_idea: Exact integer-programming solution of the linear ordering problem for maximum-likelihood rankings; the specific speedup mechanism is not given in the abstract.
Kooe7QMXgS.evidence: Revisits 9 publications spanning LLM evaluation, benchmark leaderboards, and rank aggregation, covering 48,165 ranking instances, including a released SuperGLUE leaderboard snapshot.
Kooe7QMXgS.claimed_gains: Finds provably optimal rankings for 99.93% of the instances, typically within milliseconds on a single core, while Borda, win ratios, and greedy cycle removal incur 4.8 - 13.8% higher objective cost and pick a winner no optimal ranking places first on 23 - 96% of instances.
Kooe7QMXgS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree XRank gives near-heuristic runtime without the accuracy cost, with clear math and reasonable, fair baselines and evaluations.
Kooe7QMXgS.main_concern: The abstract's claim of a fast exact solver is seen as misleading for an NP-hard problem since worst-case time stays intractable, and results may be limited to ML instances with sparse comparisons.

uOHiz39xkV.one_liner: Ensemble causal discovery that lets an LLM arbitrate only edges where algorithms disagree, weighted by annotation-free reliability estimates.
uOHiz39xkV.problem: LLM-augmented causal discovery is vulnerable to LLM errors, so it must decide when to trust LLM knowledge versus statistical evidence.
uOHiz39xkV.method: Three stages: an algorithm ensemble resolves consensus edges by voting; a trust-calibrated arbitration estimates the relative reliability of the LLM and the algorithms without annotations and runs trust-weighted voting that restricts the LLM to edges with unreliable algorithmic evidence; a cycle repair step guarantees an acyclic graph.
uOHiz39xkV.key_idea: Estimate LLM and algorithm reliability from agreement on consensus edges without annotations, then use it to weight votes only on disputed edges.
uOHiz39xkV.evidence: Experiments on six datasets, with ablation and robustness analyses mentioned in the reviews (abstract is truncated).
uOHiz39xkV.claimed_gains: Consensus voting resolves up to 96% of edges with near-perfect accuracy on the filtered consensus edges, and CauTion consistently outperforms both comparison groups (cut off in the abstract) on six datasets.
uOHiz39xkV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the calibration scheme is clearly explained and effective, combining statistical methods on consensus pairs with LLM judgment on uncertain pairs, with a decision-based justification for selective LLM querying.
uOHiz39xkV.main_concern: The key assumption that LLM reliability estimated on consensus pairs transfers to harder disputed pairs is not validated.

QhGdVnRPoi.one_liner: TCSExam benchmarks LLMs on 100 verifiable theoretical computer science tasks, including theorem proving, solver engineering, constructions, and open conjectures.
QhGdVnRPoi.problem: There is no unified benchmark to measure LLM progress toward autonomous theoretical computer science research, including attempts on open conjectures.
QhGdVnRPoi.method: A benchmark of 100 expert-reviewed tasks checked by the Lean kernel or an executable task checker, used to evaluate six frontier LLMs.
QhGdVnRPoi.key_idea: Combine formally or computationally verifiable task types in one framework, with submissions checked by the Lean kernel or executable checkers.
QhGdVnRPoi.evidence: Evaluation of six frontier LLMs on 100 tasks, including 30 open conjectures with up to 12 hours per attempt.
QhGdVnRPoi.claimed_gains: The strongest model gives complete verified proofs in 70% of attempts without a proof outline versus at most 11.7% for any other model; none of the six models resolves any of 30 open conjectures.
QhGdVnRPoi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is well constructed, covers varied task types, and offers rigorous, reproducible verification.
QhGdVnRPoi.main_concern: The contribution beyond bundling existing task types is unclear, and the benchmark is small (100 tasks, 20 on theorem proving).

9pLlsv1dAk.one_liner: Shows MoE channel selection needs no calibration: per-token top-k matches or beats calibrated thresholds, plus a weight-only ternary-sketch reader.
9pLlsv1dAk.problem: MoE decoding at small batch is bound by loading routed-expert weights, and calibrated channel thresholds neither fix the read budget nor reliably improve accuracy.
9pLlsv1dAk.method: The authors compare threshold and per-token top-k selection on the same scores, then build a reader entirely from model weights that screens channels with a ternary sketch and recovers skipped ones (abstract text cuts off here).
9pLlsv1dAk.key_idea: Keep each token's k highest-scoring channels instead of a calibrated threshold, and screen channels using a ternary sketch computed only from the model's weights.
9pLlsv1dAk.evidence: 43 top-k versus threshold comparisons at 13% and 18% read budgets across tasks, models including Gemma 4 and Qwen3 variants, and ablations of the sketch and recovery parts.
9pLlsv1dAk.claimed_gains: Top-k matches or beats the threshold version in 40 of 43 comparisons, including all 23 on generation tasks; Prox calibrated for an 18% budget reads only 12.9% on average.
9pLlsv1dAk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the isolation of ranking from the keep rule is informative and the calibration-free approach simplifies existing inference optimization.
9pLlsv1dAk.main_concern: At the sparsest budget the proposed reader trails a calibration-free Prox variant (51.0% versus 62.1% on Gemma 4 GPQA-Diamond), and read counts are analytical rather than profiled.

TvqsIaE2Lm.one_liner: Forecasting with external evidence as an action-conditioned world model whose latent actions come from a primitive bank.
TvqsIaE2Lm.problem: Existing forecasters feed external evidence as extra inputs and leave the state-dependent dynamic response implicit, although the same evidence can induce different responses depending on system state.
TvqsIaE2Lm.method: EGA-WM learns a latent action space through a primitive bank, infers state-dependent actions from external evidence, and uses them to modulate future state transitions through input modulation, retention modulation and recurrent propagation.
TvqsIaE2Lm.key_idea: Infer state-dependent latent actions from external evidence via a primitive bank and apply them as input and retention modulation of recurrent state transitions.
TvqsIaE2Lm.evidence: Per the reviews, electricity price forecasting with day-ahead load, generation or wind forecasts and retail sales datasets (Rossmann, M5), compared with Sonnet and other baselines, with ablations.
TvqsIaE2Lm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating external evidence as having state-dependent effects is well motivated and that the architecture, which separates action activation from effect persistence, is coherent.
TvqsIaE2Lm.main_concern: The base forecaster is reported inconsistently between tables, so the source of the gains is unclear (M5 MSE moves only from 1.5246 to 1.5220), and there is no evidence the module learns event-specific responses.

KTpdAjZKco.one_liner: Powered L1 attention with a per-layer sharpness exponent and signed scores replaces softmax to deepen multi-hop reasoning.
KTpdAjZKco.problem: Softmax has no parameter directly controlling attention sharpness, which depends indirectly on query-key magnitudes and varies across seeds, while sharpness is empirically associated with reasoning depth.
KTpdAjZKco.method: L1p normalizes attention with a per-layer exponent controlling sharpness and makes scores invariant to the overall magnitude of query-key products. A signed form permits negative attention scores, which ablations show is critical for reasoning depth.
KTpdAjZKco.key_idea: Replace softmax with a powered-L1 normalizer whose per-layer exponent sets sharpness, invariant to query-key magnitude, and permit negative attention scores.
KTpdAjZKco.evidence: A synthetic multi-hop task with exactly controllable hops (32 seeds per model) compared with softmax and five other normalizers, language-modeling perplexity over 24 seeds, and downstream evaluations in the appendix.
KTpdAjZKco.claimed_gains: At 4 hops, L1p solves the task in 18 of 32 seeds while every alternative succeeds in at most 3 of 32, and across 24 seeds it matches softmax language-modeling perplexity within a margin cut off in the abstract.
KTpdAjZKco.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-hop reasoning gains are large and statistically supported by many seeds and ablations, and that the mechanism is simple and interpretable.
KTpdAjZKco.main_concern: Reasoning evidence rests on a single synthetic graph-traversal task without transfer to realistic multi-step benchmarks, and the benefit of a learnable exponent is unclear since a fixed one performs comparably.

edU3ZjQloh.one_liner: A 1.31M-parameter adapter predicts the source-content condition from text so frozen audio-conditioned V2A models generate only the requested sound.
edU3ZjQloh.problem: Text-guided selective video-to-audio systems learn source selection and generation together from large, automatically constructed datasets, which is data-hungry.
edU3ZjQloh.method: In ControlFoley, an isolated reference suppresses other visible events, and a pathway intervention localizes this to an internal source-content condition. The CSIO adapter predicts this condition from target text with the generator frozen, and SelFoley adds early visual-synchronization guidance to recover timing.
edU3ZjQloh.key_idea: Source selection is controlled by an internal vector representing the reference sound's content; predict that vector from target text with a small adapter instead of training a selective generator.
edU3ZjQloh.evidence: Pathway interventions on ControlFoley, an adapter trained on StemFoleyDB-3.3K (3,357 clips, 5,383 human-audited source stems), comparison with SelVA, and use on three audio-conditioned backbones (from reviews).
edU3ZjQloh.claimed_gains: Relative to SelVA's reported 179k-video, roughly 500-hour corpus, SelFoley uses 98.2% fewer task-training clips and 96.8% fewer (quantity cut off), with 300 adapter updates.
edU3ZjQloh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the intervention analysis locating source selection in the semantic reference pathway is convincing and that the frozen-generator adapter works with little training.
edU3ZjQloh.main_concern: Generality and timing are limited: listeners rate synchronization lower than SelVA (2.94 versus 3.40), and the method works only on audio-conditioned backbones with strong reference pathways, with gains varying across them.

yYaCCwYAlk.one_liner: Unlearns knowledge-graph embedding facts by differentiating through a tangent-kernel model of how continued training would relearn them.
yYaCCwYAlk.problem: After approximate unlearning of knowledge-graph embeddings, forgotten facts recover under ordinary continued training more than in an exact-unlearning baseline, because entity embeddings are shared with new facts.
yYaCCwYAlk.method: Kernel-Anticipated Unlearning (KAU) uses the tangent kernel to model, in closed form, how continued training changes forgotten facts' scores through shared parameters, and differentiates through it inside the forgetting loss. This steers edits toward directions that continued training reverses less.
yYaCCwYAlk.key_idea: Put a closed-form tangent-kernel prediction of continued-training relearning inside the forgetting loss so edits avoid directions that new updates would undo.
yYaCCwYAlk.evidence: Three backbones on FB15k-237 and CoDEx-L, compared with knowledge-graph unlearners and relearning-robust methods under identical continued training, measuring leakage beyond the exact-unlearning baseline.
yYaCCwYAlk.claimed_gains: KAU reduces the strongest knowledge-graph unlearner's leakage by 46-63% on FB15k-237 and 50-82% on CoDEx-L, at higher retained utility.
yYaCCwYAlk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree relearning in knowledge-graph embeddings is a new, important problem and that the protocol subtracting the retrained oracle's recovery measures excess relearning meaningfully.
yYaCCwYAlk.main_concern: Evaluation scope and theory fit are limited: synthetic update scenarios with one deletion setting, no check of learning plasticity, and a linearized analysis that may not explain the Adam-trained implementation.

8vmSIFfjfb.one_liner: Builds higher-quality multi-turn RL rollouts with lightweight per-turn tree search, needing no search at inference time.
8vmSIFfjfb.problem: Multi-turn agent RL has sparse or delayed rewards and stochastic environments, so naive trajectory sampling hinders exploitation and induces mode collapse.
8vmSIFfjfb.method: TSR performs lightweight tree-style search during rollout generation, selecting promising actions and trajectory prefixes with progress-based scoring, and stays compatible with standard policy-gradient optimizers. It trades extra training-time rollout compute for a stronger policy that needs no search at inference.
8vmSIFfjfb.key_idea: Move test-time search into the rollout stage of training, choosing actions and prefixes with a scorer while leaving the optimizer and objective unchanged.
8vmSIFfjfb.evidence: Five agentic environments (including FrozenLake and WebShop per reviews) with scorer, compute, and optimizer controls, and a combination with GiGPO.
8vmSIFfjfb.claimed_gains: Success rates improve by up to 15 percentage points with progress-based scoring, per-turn search accounts for 5-6 of these points, and gains of 9-11 points persist with a learned observation-only scorer.
8vmSIFfjfb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree TSR is a simple, optimizer-agnostic intervention with consistent gains across environments and thorough controls for compute and scoring.
8vmSIFfjfb.main_concern: Gains are confounded by hand-designed, possibly privileged progress scorers, and budget-matched baselines may not use their extra compute, with unresolved selection bias and no direct Tree-GRPO comparison.

FQbfUdMJhC.one_liner: Adapts LoRA steps by covariance matching and constrains output drift on past-task feature statistics in online continual learning.
FQbfUdMJhC.problem: In online continual learning with a data stream, current-task information alone cannot show how adaptation affects earlier tasks, and task boundaries are unavailable at inference.
FQbfUdMJhC.method: RASA models optimization-induced parameter changes as a local Gaussian transition whose covariance is matched to a stream-estimated reference to set adaptive steps. It uses aggregated feature second moments from previous tasks to constrain cumulative changes in LoRA linear outputs on historical inputs, combined with current-batch gradients in a local generalized posterior.
FQbfUdMJhC.key_idea: Match the covariance of parameter changes to a stream-estimated reference to scale steps, and bound LoRA output changes on old-task inputs using stored feature second moments.
FQbfUdMJhC.evidence: Applied on top of expansion methods, SeqLoRA, and OSFT across backbones and benchmarks, with component and learning-rate analyses (from reviews).
FQbfUdMJhC.claimed_gains: The abstract gives no figures; a review cites average performance rising from 56.35 to 69.38 for Gain-OLoRA and from 39.40 to 53.44 for OSFT on Standard CL.
FQbfUdMJhC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree RASA adds no parameters, replay, or extra passes, retains data-free, and gives consistent gains across methods, backbones, and benchmarks.
FQbfUdMJhC.main_concern: It needs task boundaries during training, which limits the online claim, and the adaptive step alone accounts for most of the gain while covariance matching versus simpler adaptive scaling is not isolated.

WQ9dP3hpWs.one_liner: Formulates multimodal KG fusion as optimal transport with sliced-Wasserstein scale selection and Nash-bargaining refinement of transport plans.
WQ9dP3hpWs.problem: Multimodal knowledge-graph fusion suffers from target-irrelevant semantics and uneven modality contribution, and existing methods align all modalities indiscriminately with pre-defined fusion strategies.
WQ9dP3hpWs.method: NaCOT builds cascaded representation candidates and uses sliced Wasserstein distance selection to identify compatible source-target scales for optimal-transport alignment. A Nash bargaining fusion mechanism then refines transport plans under fusion and OT constraints.
WQ9dP3hpWs.key_idea: Choose representation scales for OT alignment by sliced Wasserstein distance, then reconcile modality utilities by Nash bargaining on the transport plans.
WQ9dP3hpWs.evidence: Four MMKG benchmarks, with ablations, noise and missing-modality robustness, encoder changes, and entity-linking transfer (from reviews).
WQ9dP3hpWs.claimed_gains: Average relative improvements of 24.68% in MRR and 23.51% in Hit@1 over the strongest baselines.
WQ9dP3hpWs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree low target relevance and modality imbalance are well motivated problems and the experiments are comprehensive.
WQ9dP3hpWs.main_concern: Low target relevance is handled only indirectly with no evidence the selected candidates are cleaner, overhead versus OTKGE is not fully accounted for, and the pseudocode and equations appear inconsistent.

DReSwYwieE.one_liner: Scores candidate actions by successor-value advantage over a quantile of behavior-induced values, correcting critic targets and guiding a diffusion actor.
DReSwYwieE.problem: Offline RL must improve on recorded behavior while controlling errors in evaluating out-of-distribution actions.
DReSwYwieE.method: ADAC compares candidate and behavior actions through successor values predicted by a learned dynamics model and evaluated by a state-value function learned from offline transitions. Subtracting a quantile of behavior-induced values from the candidate's successor value gives a signed quantile advantage that corrects critic targets and guides a diffusion actor alongside behavior cloning.
DReSwYwieE.key_idea: Evaluate a candidate by the value of its predicted successor relative to a quantile of values of successors under behavior actions, instead of penalizing out-of-distribution actions.
DReSwYwieE.evidence: 20 D4RL tasks across Gym, AntMaze, Adroit, and Kitchen, four-domain component ablations, a 15-task quantile study, and a PointMaze illustration.
DReSwYwieE.claimed_gains: ADAC achieves the highest reported mean on 15 of 20 D4RL tasks.
DReSwYwieE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using behavior-induced successor values as a reference, rather than conservative penalties, is a well-motivated idea backed by broad D4RL experiments and a PointMaze demonstration.
DReSwYwieE.main_concern: OOD-action evaluation is not directly validated: dynamics-model and value accuracy are untested and no metric shows which actions are OOD, so gains may come from better value estimation among in-distribution candidates.

Ez2fKIyYoo.one_liner: Pools attention-head value contributions across generated tokens and trains a linear probe to detect contextual hallucinations in RAG.
Ez2fKIyYoo.problem: Retrieval-augmented language models produce claims unsupported by their supplied context, and detecting such contextual hallucinations needs a reliable signal.
Ez2fKIyYoo.method: HeadAxis pools each attention head's current-value contributions across generated positions into a response-level representation and trains a linear probe to learn a hallucination-discriminating axis.
Ez2fKIyYoo.key_idea: Response-level pooling of per-head value contributions over generated tokens gives a linear axis that separates hallucinated from context-supported responses.
Ez2fKIyYoo.evidence: Multiple RAG hallucination benchmarks and model families (twelve model-dataset combinations in a review, including RAGTruth and RAGBench), with cross-dataset transfer and ablations.
Ez2fKIyYoo.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims HeadAxis consistently matches or exceeds strong white-box hallucination detectors.
Ez2fKIyYoo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the detector is simple and works across many models, datasets, and baselines, with promising cross-dataset transfer.
Ez2fKIyYoo.main_concern: Novelty and evidence strength are questioned: margins over ITI and RAGLens are small, cross-dataset transfer lacks matched baselines (RAGTruth-trained probes reach only .562 and .525 AUROC on RAGBench), and statistical tests are not reported clearly.

Okzb5CIpgH.one_liner: A non-diagonal SSM using noncommuting SO(3) rotations composed via quaternions, trainable with state-space duality.
Okzb5CIpgH.problem: Diagonal SSMs cannot solve NC^1-complete state-tracking problems, while existing non-diagonal transitions such as SLiCE and DeltaProduct raise training cost, so non-diagonal transitions need to be combined with SSD's efficient parallel training.
Okzb5CIpgH.method: Caracal uses noncommuting SO(3) rotations composed through quaternions, giving SO3SSD, which keeps scalar SSD efficiency by absorbing ordered rotation products into keys and queries. A reviewer adds that it also uses exact first-order-hold integration.
Okzb5CIpgH.key_idea: Compose per-token SO(3) rotations via quaternions and fold them into keys and queries so the noncommuting transition keeps SSD's parallel matrix-multiplication form.
Okzb5CIpgH.evidence: The A_5 benchmark with a single layer, finite-state automata, a language-model comparison (perplexity, zero-shot), MAD compression and selective copying, and training-speed measurements against Mamba-3.
Okzb5CIpgH.claimed_gains: Solves the A_5 benchmark with a single layer, reports the lowest measured test perplexities in its comparison, and trains complete language models 1.20-1.34x faster than Mamba-3 in FP32.
Okzb5CIpgH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the construction is an efficient way to add noncommuting transitions to Mamba-style SSMs and that the A_5 and FSA results convincingly show better state tracking.
Okzb5CIpgH.main_concern: The two main ingredients, noncommuting rotations and exact first-order-hold integration, are not ablated, the speed advantage depends on configuration, and state-tracking gains do not yet show up downstream.

m5NJrYCnmy.one_liner: Rao-Blackwellizes a two-query antithetic gradient estimator over block aggregates, reducing variance for aggregate-invariant black-box scores with no extra queries.
m5NJrYCnmy.problem: Optimizing differentiable models against vector-valued black-box scores is expensive when each query evaluates thousands of binary decisions, and gradient noise must fall without more oracle queries.
m5NJrYCnmy.method: Block-OSRB conditions a two-query antithetic estimator (the DisARM parent) on paired block aggregates, integrating out row identities invisible to the evaluator, using the same two oracle values for every row. For independent Bernoulli decisions it is unbiased and has no greater covariance than DisARM per output column.
m5NJrYCnmy.key_idea: Condition the DisARM-style antithetic estimator on the block aggregates the metric depends on, integrating out row identities exactly from the same two oracle values.
m5NJrYCnmy.evidence: Adult, ACSIncome, Waterbirds, and UCI Credit holdout hypervolume regret, a Student Dropout trainable-MLP test, and covariance-dominance theorems.
m5NJrYCnmy.claimed_gains: Count Block-OSRB has lower mean one-time holdout hypervolume regret in all eight task-budget cells than the evaluated DisARM and true UGC arms, with reductions of 2.0-19.7% and 2.2-23.8% respectively.
m5NJrYCnmy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exact conditioning gives provable covariance dominance over DisARM without extra oracle calls and is backed by extensive theory.
m5NJrYCnmy.main_concern: Empirical gains are overstated against a weak parent, since much of the improvement over unmasked DisARM comes from masking irrelevant rows, and the method needs independent Bernoulli decisions with a declared aggregate contract.

BwOImGdN0q.one_liner: Benchmark on life-like cellular automata testing deduction, induction and abduction on the same transitions, plus a recursive propose-then-verify agent.
BwOImGdN0q.problem: Existing reasoning benchmarks cover a single form of reasoning or lack formal grounding across deduction, induction, and abduction, so differences between forms cannot be measured in a principled way.
BwOImGdN0q.method: LifeWorld uses 2^18 life-like cellular-automata rules generalizing Conway's Game of Life, built from a rule P, a configuration, and its k-step successor, to pose deduction, induction, and abduction tasks. LifeAgent is a recursive propose-then-verify harness with space-time and logical recursion.
BwOImGdN0q.key_idea: Derive all three reasoning forms from one rule, state, and successor with programmatic verification and complexity-grounded difficulty, and attack them with a recursive propose-then-verify harness.
BwOImGdN0q.evidence: LLM evaluations on the benchmark with analyses of induction checking and abduction verification, and LifeAgent tested on one model at the hard level (from reviews); the abstract is truncated.
BwOImGdN0q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the single-environment design gives clean, verifiable, scalable tasks that make differences across the three reasoning forms comparable.
BwOImGdN0q.main_concern: Grading and harness validity are questioned: induction is graded differently from abduction and can mark valid rules wrong, uses a single observation pair, and LifeAgent is tested on one model with hyperparameter-sensitive recursion.

hphaxV0AGr.one_liner: Open EEG dataset for infantile epileptic spasms syndrome with diagnosis and treatment-response labels and foundation-model benchmarks.
hphaxV0AGr.problem: Public EEG data for infantile epileptic spasms syndrome is scarce, limiting study of EEG characteristics associated with the disorder and with treatment response.
hphaxV0AGr.method: IESSEEG releases about 3,172 hours of EEG from 100 pediatric participants with diagnosis and treatment-response labels, clinician annotations, BASED scores, and clinical metadata. It sets shared benchmarks comparing traditional qEEG methods with eight EEG foundation models.
hphaxV0AGr.key_idea: Release labelled clinical EEG with shared benchmarks and test whether combining qEEG features, learned representations, and clinical metadata improves treatment-response prediction.
hphaxV0AGr.evidence: Diagnosis and treatment-response benchmarks with qEEG methods and eight EEG foundation models under frozen and fully fine-tuned settings, using fixed patient-level splits.
hphaxV0AGr.claimed_gains: No metric values stated; the abstract reports strong diagnosis performance from both qEEG and foundation models, and harder treatment-response prediction that benefits less consistently from fine-tuning.
hphaxV0AGr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a valuable, scarce public pediatric EEG resource with a clear motivation, rigorous experimental design, and clinical research value.
hphaxV0AGr.main_concern: The cohort is small (100 participants) and shows a noticeable age gap between case and control groups (median 0.93 versus 1.52 years), with limited detail on data quality and annotation.

xXjBJrb3pJ.one_liner: Learns head-wise query aggregation and scoring so one indexer scan serves a group of queries in DeepSeek sparse attention.
xXjBJrb3pJ.problem: DeepSeek Sparse Attention's indexer scans the whole prefix for every query and dominates long-context prefill, and existing query-group sharing averages queries and loses accuracy as groups widen.
xXjBJrb3pJ.method: GroupIndex jointly learns head-wise query aggregation and scoring projections in a Surrogate Indexer and uses hardware-aware layer specialization to select each layer's query-group width and candidate budget. It then indexes each query from the shared candidates (abstract truncated).
xXjBJrb3pJ.key_idea: A shared scan must keep every key any member selects, so learn aggregation supervised by the union of members' selections instead of mean-pooling queries.
xXjBJrb3pJ.evidence: DeepSeek-V4-Flash with RULER evaluations up to 512K context, whole-prefill latency measurements, and component ablations against PIVOT-Refine (from reviews).
xXjBJrb3pJ.claimed_gains: The abstract figures are cut off; a review cites a 512K RULER score of 88.2 for GroupIndex versus 75.6 for PIVOT-Refine and 88.3 for the native baseline at g=16 and c=2048.
xXjBJrb3pJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis of mean-pooled query sharing motivates a learned union-covering surrogate, supported by ablations and real prefill speedups.
xXjBJrb3pJ.main_concern: Pooling over a whole query group may let later queries influence earlier selections, so prefix consistency is unproven, quality is checked only to 512K while the strongest speedup is at 1M, and novelty versus DefensiveKV and Quest is unclear.

lwLFqizbDm.one_liner: Benchmark where LLM agents repair injected faults in live containerized networks, judged by running network state and collateral damage.
lwLFqizbDm.problem: Existing network-troubleshooting benchmarks evaluate diagnosis rather than repair, or evaluate repair only in simplified settings far from operational networks.
lwLFqizbDm.method: NetMend is a task generator that synthesizes networks across blueprints, routing protocols, and network operating systems and injects faults. Agents start from a symptom report and use typed tools rendered as real operator commands, with correctness judged from the running network state, root-cause declaration and root-device writes scored separately, and a collateral-damage check.
lwLFqizbDm.key_idea: Judge repair from the live network state with fault-specific predicates and a collateral-damage check rather than from the agent's own report.
lwLFqizbDm.evidence: A released task bank of 29 fault classes and eight compound combinations, synthetic networks plus two production topologies rebuilt from vendor configurations, and evaluations of LLM agents (abstract truncated).
lwLFqizbDm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the executable, replayable, state-verified evaluation with a collateral-damage check and multidimensional metrics is a substantive benchmark contribution for a practical problem.
lwLFqizbDm.main_concern: The root-cause metric credits touching the right device rather than diagnosing the fault, and the benchmark is near saturation at the frontier, with 5 of 7 open-weight models above 85% and overlapping intervals.

LwclPaKZhy.one_liner: Each node attends to all nodes in each cluster from off-the-shelf community detection, augmenting message-passing networks or graph transformers.
LwclPaKZhy.problem: Message passing has a receptive field bounded by layer count, while global attention in graph transformers ignores graph topology and lacks structural inductive bias.
LwclPaKZhy.method: CLATT divides graph nodes into clusters using off-the-shelf community detection and lets each node attend to all other nodes in each cluster. It is added to message-passing networks or graph transformers without replacing their original mechanisms.
LwclPaKZhy.key_idea: Restrict attention scope to graph clusters from community detection, giving long-range interaction that stays tied to graph structure, as a modular add-on to existing backbones.
LwclPaKZhy.evidence: A wide range of graph datasets, including real-world applications from the GraphLand benchmark, with comparisons across backbones.
LwclPaKZhy.claimed_gains: The abstract gives no figures; a review reports higher mean performance in 55 of 56 completed comparisons, for example 46.41 to 49.34 for LGT on pokec-regions.
LwclPaKZhy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and modular and gives broad, consistent gains across graphs of different sizes and structure.
LwclPaKZhy.main_concern: Novelty relative to CoBFormer-style intra-cluster attention and other grouped attention is unclear, and there is no random-group control or accounting for the cost of selecting the best clustering per dataset.

OtrOIMLig8.one_liner: Million-image medical forgery benchmark plus a model distilling four frozen experts into pre-hoc analyze-localize-decide reasoning.
OtrOIMLig8.problem: Medical image forensics benchmarks are limited in scale, diversity, forgery coverage, clinical plausibility, or spatial fidelity, and methods separate detection from localization, add post-hoc explanations, or use CoT from general multimodal models without forensic evidence.
OtrOIMLig8.method: BEAR-Med-1M spans four clinical imaging categories and five mechanisms (copy-move, splicing, lesion insertion, lesion removal, full-image synthesis), using bidirectional restoration for spatially faithful local forgeries. BEAR-Med uses four frozen experts for local traces, image-wide consistency, generation texture, and medical normality, distilled offline into CoT targets so inference uses only the image.
OtrOIMLig8.key_idea: Distill evidence from four frozen forensic experts offline into CoT targets so the model reasons before localizing and deciding, with no experts needed at inference.
OtrOIMLig8.evidence: Comparisons with existing methods, ablations, robustness tests, and external evaluation including MedForge-90K, plus an audit of edits outside annotated boxes (from reviews).
OtrOIMLig8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is large and covers many modalities and manipulation types, with an outside-box audit and an offline distillation design that needs only the original image at inference.
OtrOIMLig8.main_concern: In-distribution results are near saturated while external localization is weak (Box IoU@0.75 of only 0.083 on MedForge-90K), the benchmark's contribution beyond scale is unclear, and reasoning is judged mostly by LLMs.

aBDrWF4tpW.one_liner: Adds covariance-aware phoneme-relation credit to CTC and word/sentence embedding alignment without word timings for brain-to-text decoding.
aBDrWF4tpW.problem: Standard CTC does not encode phoneme relations or supervise word- and sentence-level neural representations, and linking words to neural features is hard without annotated word timings.
aBDrWF4tpW.method: LENS combines classifier geometry with neural representation covariance to assign bounded credit to phoneme alternatives during CTC supervision. Posterior-Guided Multiscale Linguistic Alignment then couples neural features with pretrained word embeddings by model-derived soft alignment, plus utterance-level alignment with sentence representations.
aBDrWF4tpW.key_idea: Spread CTC credit to similar phonemes using classifier geometry and neural covariance, and align neural features to pretrained word and sentence embeddings using the model's own posterior soft alignment.
aBDrWF4tpW.evidence: Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 benchmarks without changing the decoding pipeline, with ablations, a CAPS to CTC control, and multiple seeds.
aBDrWF4tpW.claimed_gains: Reports best word error rates on Brain-to-Text '24 and '25; a review cites validation WER of 9.06% to 8.92% on '24 and 2.95% to 2.85% on '25 versus the CAPS to CTC model.
aBDrWF4tpW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree LENS gives strong single-model results on both benchmarks and that relaxing CTC with phoneme relations is a sound improvement that leaves the decoding architecture unchanged.
aBDrWF4tpW.main_concern: Component contributions are small and not fully isolated (no CTC to PMLA control, modest multiscale gains), CAPS may capture dataset statistics, and related work such as BrainWhisperer is missing.

wO7Bph04Ga.one_liner: Shows magnitude-only world-model action probes miss reversed responses and introduces a matched probe comparing responses with logged similar-state pairs.
wO7Bph04Ga.problem: Cheap simulator-free probes may not notice when a world model's prediction moves the wrong way in response to an action change, which planning depends on.
wO7Bph04Ga.method: Simulators that return to a saved state give the true effect of each action change, used on 92 trained robot world models and 143 released models, including reflected copies that reverse response direction at the same size. The paper proves magnitude-only probes cannot detect this and proposes a matched probe that compares the model's response with pairs of similar situations in recorded data.
wO7Bph04Ga.key_idea: Compare the model's response to an action swap against logged pairs of similar states with different actions, which carries the directional information magnitude probes lack.
wO7Bph04Ga.evidence: Proofs (with Lean-verified propositions per a review), 92 trained robot world models, 143 released models including Atari frame predictors, models predicting image features, and an MPC experiment.
wO7Bph04Ga.claimed_gains: No numeric gain stated; the matched probe tracks the true direction in all three groups of models, while the logged action retrieval probe even scores the reflected models higher.
wO7Bph04Ga.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the proofs and the reflection-transform test across 235 models convincingly show that standard probes fail, and that the paper is clear about its limitations.
wO7Bph04Ga.main_concern: The matched probe covers only action swaps present in logged data and needs similar states with different actions, so it cannot certify the off-support actions planners query.

rEfxd69VBD.one_liner: Multilevel normalizing flow samples lattice gauge plaquettes coarse-to-fine, satisfying Bianchi constraints exactly through local constraint solves.
rEfxd69VBD.problem: Generative samplers in link space face long-range correlations at weak coupling, while plaquette variables suit the local action but lie on a lower-dimensional manifold defined by exact Bianchi constraints that complicate direct modeling.
rEfxd69VBD.method: A multilevel normalizing-flow construction samples directly in plaquette space with a coarse-to-fine factorization, so each determined plaquette depends on at most four newly generated variables and the constraint problem size is independent of lattice size. It is validated for U(1) in two dimensions and beyond (abstract truncated).
rEfxd69VBD.key_idea: Turn the global Bianchi constraint into a sequence of local solves in which each determined plaquette depends on at most four newly generated variables.
rEfxd69VBD.evidence: 2D U(1), 4D U(1), and 2D SU(2) lattices per reviews, compared with single-level plaquette sampling and link-space baselines, with topological susceptibility and Wilson-loop checks.
rEfxd69VBD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multilevel construction keeps exact constraint satisfaction and density evaluation while making constraint solves local, and improves on single-level and link-space baselines.
rEfxd69VBD.main_concern: Scale and baselines are limited: only small lattices (4D only 2^4 to 4^4) with single training runs, few compared methods, and no clear evidence for the conditioning mechanism or for wider use on other constrained sampling problems.

osWlOiWQDI.one_liner: Secant-based ambient-space integrators for Riemannian manifold HMC on hierarchical-model posteriors, including RATTLE as a special case.
osWlOiWQDI.problem: Every RMHMC integration step requires solving an implicit system containing derivatives of the metric, which is costly and sensitive to curvature.
osWlOiWQDI.method: For hierarchical models with a diffeomorphic map from a standard normal xi to (q,x), conditioning on x restricts xi to a submanifold with chart q. Variational integrators are rewritten in ambient coordinates, making them reparameterization-invariant, to give a secant version of each implicit integrator, and RATTLE is shown to equal the Generalized Leapfrog in ambient space.
osWlOiWQDI.key_idea: Integrate along secants in the ambient space of xi, rewriting the kinetic term in ambient coordinates so steps do not depend on the manifold's curvature or parameterization.
osWlOiWQDI.evidence: Eight solvers for six implicit integrators on four test problems, including Neal's funnel, a supernova dust emission model, and a hierarchical Gaussian process.
osWlOiWQDI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the contribution is clearly explained and conceptually simple, with detailed, carefully organized numerical experiments on a clearly identified practical difficulty.
osWlOiWQDI.main_concern: The conclusions rest only on experiments with no theory for validity or complexity, and comparisons between standard RMHMC and ambient secants are limited and less conclusive than claimed.

Fy56kk8SBB.one_liner: A multi-agent vehicle/route-state interface pretrains one routing policy across 16 CVRP variants for frozen or fine-tuned transfer.
Fy56kk8SBB.problem: Routing foundation models must transfer one pretrained policy when constraints, fleets or objectives change across vehicle routing variants.
Fy56kk8SBB.method: A multi-agent interface organized around vehicle and partial-route states and route-customer extensions, with allocation-driven rollouts that diversify pretraining of separate source backbones on 16 CVRP variants. Transfer is evaluated weight-frozen (with supplied constraint features and feasibility masks) and by fine-tuning with new vehicle attributes and objectives; route-slot tokens and a geometric prior are linked to multi-depot transfer.
Fy56kk8SBB.key_idea: Frame route construction as multi-agent extensions of partial routes by vehicles, with route-slot tokens and a geometric prior to carry multi-depot transfer.
Fy56kk8SBB.evidence: Weight-frozen transfer on 32 unseen variants and CVRPLib instances, fine-tuning against adapted multi-task baselines, and a three-seed pretrained-versus-scratch comparison.
Fy56kk8SBB.claimed_gains: Frozen reuse gives a 17.19% mean gap on 32 unseen variants at N=100 against 34.89% for the strongest baseline (27.21% with all depots encoded), with the lowest gap on 28 of them and the lowest neural gap on 37/65 CVRPLib instances; pretrained fine-tuning at 200K target exposures reaches lower mean cost than scratch training at 1M in each of three fleet settings.
Fy56kk8SBB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pretrained initialization beats training from scratch under the same architecture and that the frozen-transfer results are promising, with a well-written paper and comprehensive ablations.
Fy56kk8SBB.main_concern: Transfer gains are not isolated from the multi-agent interface (no route-by-route comparison under the same backbone, prior and training), the multi-depot baseline features and masks may not be consistent, and a closely related distance-prior method is not compared.

TDG1twoyxC.one_liner: Ordered categories lie along an ordinal axis in the residual stream, recoverable from endpoint activations and used in category comparisons.
TDG1twoyxC.problem: Accounts of concept geometry cover continuous, cyclic and unordered categorical concepts but not how conventional orders, such as viscount versus baron, are represented.
TDG1twoyxC.method: An ordinal axis is fitted from the activations of the two endpoint categories alone and tested on whether it places held-out intermediate categories in order across several models and domains. Causal tests exchange two categories' coordinates along this direction, then compare against a trained causal direction decomposed into the ordinal axis plus the gradient of the answer logits.
TDG1twoyxC.key_idea: Fit an axis from endpoint-category activations; swapping coordinates along it flips comparisons, and adding the answer-logit gradient recovers much of a trained causal direction's effect.
TDG1twoyxC.evidence: Several language models and many domains (ranks, titles, physical scales), with interventions compared against random directions of the same size and a trained DAS direction.
TDG1twoyxC.claimed_gains: Exchanging coordinates along the axis flips about a third of the decisions the model gets right, whereas random directions of the same size flip far fewer.
TDG1twoyxC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the work clear and well organized, with careful intervention controls, and value the endpoint-only axis construction and the decomposition of the trained direction.
TDG1twoyxC.main_concern: Pretraining exposure is uncontrolled, so the results cannot separate an emergent representation of order from memorized ordering facts.

BBTGt5IzyY.one_liner: Shows attention-graph KV eviction is a causal HITS, proves single-hop scores lose multi-hop bridge tokens, and introduces BridgeBench.
BBTGt5IzyY.problem: Heavy-hitter and single-hop question-dependent KV-eviction scores can drop the intermediate bridge tokens needed for multi-hop reasoning in long contexts, and graph-centrality scores lack theory.
BBTGt5IzyY.method: Shows Stream-Influence is a one-pass causal form of Kleinberg's HITS, gives a bounded alternative to its divergent unnormalised recursion, and proves a symmetry theorem that single-hop question-dependent scores (H2O, SnapKV, StreamingLLM, Stream-Influence) cannot separate a gold bridge from its twin. BridgeBench, with known bridges, tests this under physical cache pruning, and a beam-restricted walk is also proposed (details truncated in the provided abstract).
BBTGt5IzyY.key_idea: Treat attention-based KV importance as causal HITS authority and show any score seeing the question through one hop cannot separate a gold bridge token from its twin.
BBTGt5IzyY.evidence: Theory on bridge-chain graphs plus BridgeBench with known bridges, evaluated under physical cache eviction on 3B-14B LLMs, with additional public-benchmark experiments.
BBTGt5IzyY.claimed_gains: Unseeded scores retain at most 8% of full-cache accuracy at a 10% budget and 21% at a 20% budget under physical eviction on 3B-14B models.
BBTGt5IzyY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the causal-HITS view and symmetry analysis give useful diagnostic insight into why existing KV eviction loses multi-hop evidence, supported by a controlled benchmark.
BBTGt5IzyY.main_concern: The CentralKV reproduction departs from its per-head graph design and some stated theorems have proof gaps, weakening the conclusions about existing methods.

qMAx40LIRn.one_liner: Excludes grammar-invalid candidates during speculative-decoding tree allocation, with cached parser-state masks shared across branches and rounds.
qMAx40LIRn.problem: In structured generation, grammar checks come after tree allocation, so 73-77% of non-root slots in EAGLE3 trees hold grammar-invalid candidates ("semantic waste").
qMAx40LIRn.method: SemanticTree excludes unreachable candidates during tree allocation while preserving the proposer's scores and budget. A parser-state mask cache shares work across branches and rounds, verification reuses the drafting masks, and it is integrated with EAGLE3 and DDTree.
qMAx40LIRn.key_idea: Mask grammar-invalid candidates out of draft-tree allocation using a cached parser-state mask so the budget goes only to reachable tokens.
qMAx40LIRn.evidence: 35 drafter-target-workload settings at batch size one with EAGLE3 and DDTree, plus a cache ablation on Qwen3-4B/Nexus; workloads include BFCL, Nexus, and ToolHop per reviews.
qMAx40LIRn.claimed_gains: Verification rounds fall by 16.4-29.8% with EAGLE3 and 17.2-25.8% with DDTree; decode throughput rises by 19.5-40.3% and 15.5-25.6%, respectively.
qMAx40LIRn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a well-motivated systems contribution that cuts verification rounds and raises throughput at the same budget, with an informative cache ablation.
qMAx40LIRn.main_concern: Evidence covers only greedy decoding on JSON tool-call workloads with length-matched sample filtering, and the core idea is seen as a modest extension.

suuS1hWSAs.one_liner: Selects state-dependent risk maps via empirical planning, fits a neural critic, and audits adherence to the selected valuation.
suuS1hWSAs.problem: Shared risk functionals such as time-dependent mixtures of CVaR cannot implement some outer-optimal policies, and it is hard to verify that a learned controller follows its selected valuation.
suuS1hWSAs.method: Proves a stationary state-dependent risk map implements an outer-optimal policy that no time-dependent, state-independent mixture of positive-level CVaR supports in a constructed problem family. The learning procedure selects risk maps by empirical planning and separate outer-objective evaluation, fits a critic, and audits using action-margin uncertainty to guide data collection.
suuS1hWSAs.key_idea: Let the risk functional vary with state and separate selecting a risk map (utility) from certifying the controller follows it (fidelity) through uncertainty-guided audit sampling.
suuS1hWSAs.evidence: A separation proof on a constructed problem family, controlled graph experiments, an independent audit, financial applications, and NASA maintenance datasets.
suuS1hWSAs.claimed_gains: Guided allocation reduces capped audit observations by 21.1% relative to uniform sampling, and on three maintenance tasks mean utility exceeds pooled direct planning with paired confidence intervals supporting gains on two.
suuS1hWSAs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find state-dependent risk an important topic and credit the separation result and the utility-versus-fidelity distinction as concrete, novel contributions.
suuS1hWSAs.main_concern: Evidence does not show when adaptive risk maps beat direct utility planning, which also reaches the optimum in controlled experiments, and the paper is dense with undefined jargon.

ndmobmgjMh.one_liner: Host-backed full KV storage with demand-sized GPU pools and on-demand fetching preserves exact sparse attention during long-context RL rollouts.
ndmobmgjMh.problem: During long-context agentic RL rollouts, sequences idle in tool waits consume most GPU KV memory, yet eviction or approximation cannot be applied without perturbing sparse top-k selection and changing the optimized policy.
ndmobmgjMh.method: Coarse KV residency stores each sequence's complete KV state in host memory while keeping a bounded GPU pool per sequence, layer, and KV group sized at admission from measured sparse-attention demand and maintained via warm-start seeding, LRU retention, and periodic reallocation. Missing entries chosen by the model's unmodified top-k selector are fetched from host memory before attention reads them.
ndmobmgjMh.key_idea: Store complete KV states on the host and maintain demand-sized per-layer GPU pools with LRU retention and periodic reallocation, fetching missing top-k entries on demand for bit-exact decoding.
ndmobmgjMh.evidence: Evaluated via production turn-structure replay and experiments on Qwen3.5-4B across sixteen registered noninferiority endpoints, oracle allocation comparisons, and cache-policy ablations.
ndmobmgjMh.claimed_gains: On Qwen3.5-4B, pooled decoding is bit-exact and passes all sixteen noninferiority endpoints while staying within 2.5–13% of oracle allocation, cutting K/V traffic by 25.7% and replacements by 40.3%, and yielding up to 88% higher aggregate decode throughput.
ndmobmgjMh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the exact correctness boundary preserving top-k candidate sets and log-probabilities, supported by sparse-attention demand profiling and cache-management ablations.
ndmobmgjMh.main_concern: Reviewers note that only the zero-lead configuration passes all quality endpoints (forgoing prefetch speedup) and that the 88% throughput gain comes from separate batch-scaling projections rather than end-to-end agentic RL rollouts with offload overhead.

oUED8T9YFR.one_liner: Coarse-to-fine attention routing and parent-guided local window denoising preserve global object semantics in training-free long-horizon compositional diffusion.
oUED8T9YFR.problem: Overlapping-window compositional diffusion achieves seamless visual joints on long-horizon outputs while often failing global semantics by duplicating or misplacing requested objects across windows.
oUED8T9YFR.method: Hierarchical Latent Cascades runs a forward pass of the pretrained diffusion model on a coarse global view to measure how parts of the condition distribute across local horizons and reweights child-window conditions down a tree. Each child window denoises under its routed local condition and its parent's estimate before sibling windows are aggregated level by level without training or external planners.
oUED8T9YFR.key_idea: Use coarse-view diffusion attention to reweight and route local conditions down a window hierarchy while conditioning child-window denoising on parent latent estimates.
oUED8T9YFR.evidence: Evaluated without training on 100 panorama prompts and 50 40-second video stories (twice native single-pass length) against coherence-oriented window samplers and one-pass generation.
oUED8T9YFR.claimed_gains: HLC raises full-prompt success from 0% for coherence-oriented samplers to 45% on 100 panorama prompts and succeeds on 74% of 50 40-second video stories versus 64% (not significant) for one-pass generation.
oUED8T9YFR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a clear gap between visual seam coherence and global semantic accuracy and addresses it with an intuitive, training-free hierarchical routing method.
oUED8T9YFR.main_concern: Reviewers cite small evaluation sample sizes (such as two base video stories and limited panorama runs) lacking statistical power, low absolute semantic success relative to external planners, and overlap with prior attention-based local prompting.

umT7r9NgxM.one_liner: Forecasting multiscale wavelet-magnitude envelopes to condition spatial attention and temporal-difference skip connections sharpens deterministic precipitation nowcasting.
umT7r9NgxM.problem: Deterministic precipitation nowcasting models smooth out rapidly evolving, high-intensity local radar echo structures as forecast lead time grows.
umT7r9NgxM.method: DySP extracts multiscale spectral envelopes by locally averaging wavelet detail magnitudes and forecasts latent spectral priors and future envelopes across lead times. A prior-guided spatiotemporal block conditions spatial attention queries and keys on latent priors and gates outputs with envelope embeddings, while temporal-difference skip connections supply high-resolution features and recent changes to the decoder.
umT7r9NgxM.key_idea: Forecast locally pooled multiscale wavelet-magnitude envelopes to condition and gate spatiotemporal attention while injecting high-resolution observation changes through temporal-difference skip connections.
umT7r9NgxM.evidence: Supported by temporal-coherence comparisons of wavelet envelopes versus signed coefficients and evaluated on the Shanghai, CIKM, and SEVIR precipitation nowcasting datasets.
umT7r9NgxM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that locally pooled wavelet-magnitude envelopes offer a clear multiscale representation that preserves sharp, intense precipitation echoes across three radar benchmarks.
umT7r9NgxM.main_concern: Reviewers question baseline comparability due to reflectivity-scaling differences and omitted training hyperparameters, incomplete isolation of linear-projection envelope forecasting, and missing loss equations in the main text.

ukuSGDZQIA.one_liner: Closed-form Bayesian posterior updates over a learned mixture prior infer uncertainty-aware user states to condition frozen LLMs online.
ukuSGDZQIA.problem: Online LLM personalization methods retrieve or summarize sparse user histories without modeling preference uncertainty or disentangling personal preferences from input-context effects.
ukuSGDZQIA.method: BayUSI treats deviations from input-conditioned population predictions as personal evidence and combines them with a learned Gaussian mixture prior via closed-form Bayesian updates over each user's history. Posterior uncertainty governs estimate revisions and provides query-specific prefix conditioning for a frozen LLM trained through its prediction loss without per-user fine-tuning.
ukuSGDZQIA.key_idea: Apply closed-form Bayesian updates over a learned mixture prior using deviations from population predictions to condition a frozen LLM with uncertainty-weighted user-preference posteriors.
ukuSGDZQIA.evidence: Evaluated on four LaMP personalization tasks across sparse and evolving user histories alongside component and mixture-size ablations.
ukuSGDZQIA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling preference uncertainty via closed-form Bayesian updates over sparse histories provides a coherent, clearly explained mechanism for conditioning frozen LLMs.
ukuSGDZQIA.main_concern: Reviewers note that a single Gaussian prior performs comparably to a multi-component mixture in several settings, preferences are assumed stationary without drift tests, and custom online LaMP splits plus similarity to ALPaCA limit comparison and originality.

l09sNgBLr9.one_liner: Combining exact local block attention with adaptive cluster-mean key aggregation enables drop-in approximate attention and linear-cost training.
l09sNgBLr9.problem: Adaptive vector-quantized attention still incurs quadratic training cost and approximates nearby token interactions coarsely through learned codewords.
l09sNgBLr9.method: AVQ-Attention-2 merges adaptive vector-quantized global attention with exact local block attention and attends to the mean of each cluster's keys instead of a codeword while correcting for double counting. Direct gradients through cluster means lower attention training complexity from O(N^2) to O(NM) and allow drop-in replacement in pretrained transformers without fine-tuning.
l09sNgBLr9.key_idea: Pair exact local window attention with adaptive global key-cluster mean aggregation, removing codeword straight-through paths to achieve O(NM) training and inference.
l09sNgBLr9.evidence: Evaluated across sequence lengths on image and video transformers against VQ-Attention, AVQ-Attention, and FlashAttention dense baselines with component and kernel ablations.
l09sNgBLr9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that attending to cluster key means alongside exact local tiles with double-counting correction is a clean improvement over AVQ-Attention with strong speed-accuracy tradeoffs.
l09sNgBLr9.main_concern: All three reviewers cite missing comparisons and discussion of closely related local-plus-global efficient attention methods such as Scatterbrain, SVG-EAR, Agent Attention, and Fast Multipole Attention.

Ta2WxQVUhI.one_liner: Visual Canaries vary secret-field rendering and inference context to probe memorization and retrieval in document vision-language models.
Ta2WxQVUhI.problem: Whole-page resolution changes confound the relationship between sensitive-field legibility and detectable memorization in document models.
Ta2WxQVUhI.method: Synthetic identifier-secret documents and matched no-canary controls isolate glyph rendering changes while holding targets, exposure, and token counts fixed. A separate fixed-weight intervention changes inference context to test page-dependent secret retrieval.
Ta2WxQVUhI.key_idea: Independently vary secret glyph legibility and inference context against matched no-canary controls to measure detectable memorization and retrieval.
Ta2WxQVUhI.evidence: Experiments on three released VLMs include rendering, corruption, duplication, backbone, and deliberate donor-pairing checks.
Ta2WxQVUhI.claimed_gains: On Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct, reducing transcription accuracy from 1.00 to 0.11 raises the memorisation gap from +0.24 to +3.63 [+3.00, +4.26] bits, while page-conditioned donor pairing enables one-query extraction for 96.0% of Qwen and 90.0% of SmolVLM canaries.
Ta2WxQVUhI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled field-level interventions and evidence that training-like page context can expose secrets missed by text-only probing.
Ta2WxQVUhI.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate legibility as the causal driver of memorization from corruption-specific training effects and retrieval accessibility.

fPd81j2qFv.one_liner: Data-only dependence certificates bound downstream fairness gaps, while Shapley values attribute full-feature-set leakage across input features.
fPd81j2qFv.problem: Data auditors often lack access to downstream models or predictions needed for conventional fairness auditing.
fPd81j2qFv.method: The framework attaches stage-local dependence certificates to feature sets in a staged pipeline using only data variables. Mutual-information and conditional-mutual-information certificates bound downstream leakage and fairness gaps, while Shapley values allocate full-set certificates as attributions.
fPd81j2qFv.key_idea: Bound downstream sensitive-attribute leakage using feature-set dependence and distribute the full-set certificate through Shapley attributions.
fPd81j2qFv.evidence: One-sided information-theoretic guarantees accompany benchmarks of 26 measures on seven datasets with robustness checks across seven downstream predictors.
fPd81j2qFv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value fairness auditing under realistic information-access constraints.
fPd81j2qFv.main_concern: Feature-set guarantees do not directly justify individual-feature certificates or all dependence measures used in the empirical evaluation.

pRmmj8CNc0.one_liner: GA-NAR derives nonlinear-response geometry descriptors and uses them to allocate neural nonlinear computation across subspaces and depth.
pRmmj8CNc0.problem: Fixed nonlinear computation in supervised surrogates does not adapt to changes in physical response intensity and subspace allocation.
pRmmj8CNc0.method: Nonlinear Response Geometry Decomposition identifies a recurring dominant response subspace and state-dependent intensity and allocation. Geometry-Adaptive Nonlinear Representation uses these descriptors to organize nonlinear computation across subspaces and network layers.
pRmmj8CNc0.key_idea: Map physical response geometry descriptors into subspace-specific and layer-wise modulation of neural nonlinear computation.
