pRmmj8CNc0.evidence: Descriptor recovery and factorial experiments span five systems, while full-framework tests cover IEEE-118, Kuramoto-64, and nonlinear heat FEM across 18 activation-system comparisons.
pRmmj8CNc0.claimed_gains: GA-NAR reduces standardized test MSE in all 18 activation-system comparisons, with median reductions of 11.5%, 2.1%, and 2.8% on IEEE-118, Kuramoto-64, and nonlinear heat FEM, respectively.
pRmmj8CNc0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the physical response geometry motivation and the structured evaluation of individual components and the complete framework.
pRmmj8CNc0.main_concern: The controls do not sufficiently establish that physics-derived descriptors justify the added architecture complexity and observed gains.

TnxNM3bO7e.one_liner: Per-batch group prices, exact route selection, and joint rounding bound expert-group loads in mixture-of-experts routing.
TnxNM3bO7e.problem: Limiting the number of expert groups per token does not prevent per-group overload, dropped assignments, or parallel execution bottlenecks.
TnxNM3bO7e.method: The analysis represents routes by their expert counts per group and characterizes score optimality and limitations of existing routing rules. A linear program sets per-batch group prices, then exact route selection and joint rounding enforce bounded deviations from load targets.
TnxNM3bO7e.key_idea: Set group prices with a per-batch linear program and jointly round split-token routes to limit each group's load deviation.
TnxNM3bO7e.evidence: Optimality and impossibility proofs accompany a batch-size-independent rounding guarantee and real-text decoding and prefill evaluations of HYPERSPACE.
TnxNM3bO7e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the analysis of deployed routing rules and the provable per-batch load guarantees.
TnxNM3bO7e.main_concern: Large routing overhead and absent end-to-end timing leave the practical speed benefit of improved load balance unproven.

uqxHtJyqpt.one_liner: Coupled Kronecker factors approximate full-matrix Adagrad using Loewner-order constraints and LogDet divergence.
uqxHtJyqpt.problem: Existing Kronecker-factored optimizers lack a complete online regret analysis for jointly developed preconditioner factors.
uqxHtJyqpt.method: The paper derives a regret bound from a Loewner-order constraint and connects approximation quality to LogDet divergence from full-matrix Adagrad. It recovers Shampoo-KL through full coupling and proposes partial coupling with the same matrix-multiplication count as Shampoo.
uqxHtJyqpt.key_idea: Jointly update Kronecker preconditioner factors toward full-matrix Adagrad under a Loewner-order constraint and LogDet approximation criterion.
uqxHtJyqpt.evidence: The work proves regret bounds for fully and partially coupled variants and evaluates multiple architectures using AlgoPerf, including LibriSpeech Conformer.
uqxHtJyqpt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the regret framework and the partially coupled design's computational appeal.
uqxHtJyqpt.main_concern: The missing direct comparison with KL-Shampoo leaves the added value over this closely related coupled optimizer unclear.

agILwX3q6v.one_liner: Persistent claim-and-reasoning graphs organize scientific literature for source-grounded retrieval and question answering.
agILwX3q6v.problem: Agentic science needs reusable, traceable scientific reasoning that supports concurrent access and incremental knowledge growth.
agILwX3q6v.method: LKM extracts persistent claim nodes with reasoning chains and sources, linking papers through question, workflow, and evidence views. Its retrieval system returns claims together with their supporting reasoning and preserves existing object identities as papers enter the collection.
agILwX3q6v.key_idea: Represent literature as addressable claim nodes with source-linked reasoning chains, then retrieve those objects and extend cross-paper links incrementally.
agILwX3q6v.evidence: Evaluations cover evidence recall on SciFact-Open and reasoning-graph ablations on ScholarQABench, alongside citation quality and scientific question answering.
agILwX3q6v.claimed_gains: LKM reports 818 retrieved supporting and contradicting evidence items on SciFact-Open, described as nearly double the comparison count in the truncated abstract.
agILwX3q6v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the scale and provenance-aware representation, with evaluations aligned to retrieval and scientific question answering.
agILwX3q6v.main_concern: Retrieval and single-turn QA evaluations do not establish the broader claimed capabilities for agentic scientific research.

T0b4fgyHFg.one_liner: Embodied Agent Arena separates local estimation and grounding from complete robotic goal execution across five capability domains.
T0b4fgyHFg.problem: Strong local VLM capabilities do not establish reliable completion of general robotic tasks.
T0b4fgyHFg.method: The arena combines existing sources with GeoProbe using a minimal harness that preserves source observations and operations. It separates metric precision, functional grounding, and native goal completion while comparing richer observations and multi-round review.
T0b4fgyHFg.key_idea: Evaluate the same agents across distinct embodied capabilities while keeping local accuracy metrics separate from terminal task success.
T0b4fgyHFg.evidence: Seven VLMs are evaluated on 1,000 cases from 32 established sources and GeoProbe across geometry, spatial reasoning, affordance, planning, and manipulation.
T0b4fgyHFg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate broad cross-domain evaluation and the separation of accurate intermediate behavior from completed goals.
T0b4fgyHFg.main_concern: The unified arena's additional methodological value beyond repackaging existing benchmarks is insufficiently established.

cv5gJ04gPo.one_liner: Geometry-coupled Gaussian and Bernoulli diffusion jointly generate articulated hand motion and binary surface contact.
cv5gJ04gPo.problem: Putting continuous motion and discrete contact in one shared continuous space ignores their different structures and correspondences.
cv5gJ04gPo.method: DisContact uses Gaussian DDPM for hand motion and Bernoulli D3PM for per-vertex contact, with stationary contact frequencies estimated empirically. Differentiable MANO geometry conditions contact denoising, while pooled contact features refine motion and structured denoisers use mesh and anatomical regions.
cv5gJ04gPo.key_idea: Couple continuous motion diffusion and discrete contact diffusion through vertex-aligned MANO geometry at every denoising step.
cv5gJ04gPo.evidence: HoloAssist and ARCTIC experiments include state-space controls, geometry-coupling ablations, and object-free motion-contact consistency diagnostics.
cv5gJ04gPo.claimed_gains: DisContact raises contact F1 on ARCTIC from 0.41 to 0.59.
cv5gJ04gPo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the native motion/contact state spaces, explicit geometric correspondence, and improvements across two datasets.
cv5gJ04gPo.main_concern: Object-free consistency metrics do not verify physically valid contact placement, penetration, or compatibility with actual objects.

LfGUcCJZvU.one_liner: FragMem recomposes historical per-label classifier rows to recall new combinations of previously observed federated concept fragments.
LfGUcCJZvU.problem: Whole-model memories cannot directly retrieve unseen concepts assembled from familiar class-level rules.
LfGUcCJZvU.method: FragMem stores multiple historical slots per label across clients and rounds, selecting slots using per-label feature moments and opening new ones via a split-half chi-squared threshold. Selected rows form a client head, and updates are averaged by label and slot.
LfGUcCJZvU.key_idea: Store historical class-state classifier rows separately and compose a head by selecting one matching state for each label.
LfGUcCJZvU.evidence: Constructed drift schedules use frozen CIFAR-100, GTSRB, and 20 Newsgroups features, with negative controls and stress tests for state overlap and imbalance.
LfGUcCJZvU.claimed_gains: FragMem stays within 0.3 points of a class-state oracle and beats memory-free refits by 4.4 to 8.3 points, tuned whole-head baselines by 4.6 to 6.9 points, and best-stored head selection by 4.7 to 6.3 points.
LfGUcCJZvU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the known-fragments/new-combinations framing and explicit analysis of memory granularity and failure conditions.
LfGUcCJZvU.main_concern: Baseline protocols and incomplete comparisons make the added value of fragment memory over existing adaptation methods difficult to isolate.

KtE4Kpl7RS.one_liner: AnswerProbe generates attention-controlled readings, then selects complete answers using native model belief and source support.
KtE4Kpl7RS.problem: Models can misread supplied passages, while context deletion changes question encoding and tokenwise decisions commit before full answers exist.
KtE4Kpl7RS.method: AnswerProbe changes only answer-token attention, sharing one prefill across batched alternative readings. Complete answers are ranked by unmodified-model belief plus source support measured through containment, entailment, or an interventional likelihood ratio.
KtE4Kpl7RS.key_idea: Preserve prompt states while varying answer attention, then use complete candidate answers to assess source support before selection.
KtE4Kpl7RS.evidence: Evaluation covers all 62,316 MRQA questions across five models, with reading and answer-selection ablations.
KtE4Kpl7RS.claimed_gains: AnswerProbe gains 3.0–4.2 F1 over greedy decoding and 2.1–2.3 F1 over the strongest published baseline.
KtE4Kpl7RS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize broad model evaluation and consistently positive results for the probing approach.
KtE4Kpl7RS.main_concern: Baselines lack the same answer-level verifier, confounding gains from alternative readings with gains from source-based selection.

B89z3BkMJN.one_liner: Adaptive layerwise smoothing transforms reduce quantization error during quantization-aware language-model training.
B89z3BkMJN.problem: Low-precision training still incurs accuracy loss despite its potential cost savings.
B89z3BkMJN.method: The approach adaptively learns smoothing matrices for each layer's matrix multiplication to reduce quantization error. Its training design addresses changing statistics, unstable quantization bases, and biased backward estimates.
B89z3BkMJN.key_idea: Update data-adaptive smoothing transforms during training so each matrix multiplication remains easier to quantize.
B89z3BkMJN.evidence: Experiments span quantized LLM pretraining, fine-tuning, and distillation, including INT4 and INT3 pretraining from 200M to 3B parameters.
B89z3BkMJN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge consistent empirical improvements across model sizes and training settings.
B89z3BkMJN.main_concern: Comparative evidence does not fully isolate the adaptive transforms, particularly where INT3 baselines use different quantization grouping.

Yv0u1TCep4.one_liner: Equivariant Cartesian perception conditions atomwise local-coordinate generation while analytic Jacobians retain evaluable molecular proposal densities.
Yv0u1TCep4.problem: Boltzmann generators must scale beyond small molecules while representing symmetries and retaining densities for statistical correction.
Yv0u1TCep4.method: SEAL-BG uses a causal SE(3)-equivariant encoder over previously generated Cartesian atoms. Normalized bond-length, bond-angle, and periodic-torsion conditionals generate subsequent atoms, with analytic local Jacobians yielding Cartesian densities.
Yv0u1TCep4.key_idea: Separate equivariant Cartesian conditioning from normalized local-coordinate generation and convert densities through analytic Jacobians.
Yv0u1TCep4.evidence: Evaluation covers four released peptide benchmarks and larger Trp-cage and Homeodomain proteins, including a 947-atom system.
Yv0u1TCep4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating geometric perception from local-coordinate density generation and extending evaluation to larger proteins.
Yv0u1TCep4.main_concern: Missing coverage and importance-weight diagnostics leave uncertainty about whether corrected metrics reflect broad Boltzmann-target overlap.

nC9nOCTEfO.one_liner: Dirichlet-process data randomization produces single-network Thompson-sampling surrogates for exploration beyond observed regions.
nC9nOCTEfO.problem: Approximate weight-space Bayesian neural networks can lose uncertainty in unobserved regions and trap black-box optimizers.
nC9nOCTEfO.method: DP-TS places a Dirichlet-process prior on the data-generating distribution and uses its push-forward over objective functions. Bayesian-bootstrap reweighting and prior hypotheses from the base measure randomize a single neural surrogate for Thompson sampling.
nC9nOCTEfO.key_idea: Randomize observed-data weights and generative prior hypotheses under a data-space Dirichlet process to sample neural surrogate functions.
nC9nOCTEfO.evidence: Benchmarks cover multimodal functions, neural hyperparameter optimization, deceptive double funnels, and high-dimensional control, including 32D and 60D tasks.
nC9nOCTEfO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple single-network uncertainty approach and evaluation of difficult exploration settings.
nC9nOCTEfO.main_concern: Claims of exact posterior sampling and the uncertainty and regret guarantees contain unjustified theoretical steps.

FGJ3r1QGNK.one_liner: Reinforcement learning prepares teachers to continue student-generated reasoning prefixes before on-policy distillation.
FGJ3r1QGNK.problem: Teachers that solve problems well independently can provide unreliable continuations of divergent or erroneous student reasoning.
FGJ3r1QGNK.method: Prep-OPD trains a teacher with reinforcement learning on fixed student-generated prefixes, rewarding final-answer correctness. The prepared teacher then guides student trajectories and supplies token-level supervision during distillation.
FGJ3r1QGNK.key_idea: Optimize teacher continuations from student-induced reasoning states before using that teacher for on-policy student supervision.
FGJ3r1QGNK.evidence: Evaluation uses eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks, a Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 teacher, Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B students, and teacher-preparation controls.
FGJ3r1QGNK.claimed_gains: With the 4B teacher and 1.7B student, average accuracy improves by 8.28 percentage points over standard OPD and 2.30 over Relay-OPD.
FGJ3r1QGNK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the intuitive preparation strategy and controlled evidence that continuation capability differs from independent problem solving.
FGJ3r1QGNK.main_concern: Efficiency claims omit or insufficiently document the extra teacher-preparation cost in end-to-end training comparisons.

2LIXTEtIJN.one_liner: Shared and capability-specific diffusion-transformer experts unify world prediction and action generation with adaptive interface routing.
2LIXTEtIJN.problem: Separately trained world and world-action models limit dynamics reuse while requiring distinct conditional capabilities.
2LIXTEtIJN.method: UniW(A)M combines shared dynamics experts with atomic capability experts reused across world-action interfaces. A lightweight supervised target-domain router selects interfaces at chunk level while the backbone remains frozen.
2LIXTEtIJN.key_idea: Share dynamics through common experts while preserving interface-specific conditional pathways through reusable capability experts.
2LIXTEtIJN.evidence: Evaluation covers LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, WorldArena, three real-world manipulation tasks, and action-conditioned world-model co-training ablations.
2LIXTEtIJN.claimed_gains: UniW(A)M achieves 88.3% average real-world success versus 76.7% for the strongest baseline.
2LIXTEtIJN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate simulation and real-robot coverage and evidence that world-model co-training benefits action interfaces.
2LIXTEtIJN.main_concern: The necessity of jointly maintaining multiple action interfaces and the specific expert decomposition is not isolated from simpler unified alternatives.

p6OGa5n0eQ.one_liner: Stored demonstrations define passage-entry gates that preserve successful approach geometry after local replanning and route recovery.
p6OGa5n0eQ.problem: Collision-free detours can approach stairs or ledges outside the entry conditions supported by a fixed locomotion skill.
p6OGa5n0eQ.method: Passage-conditioned navigation stores successful taught crossings as route events and checks approach position and direction after local replanning. An entry gate requires turning, backing up, or retrying when deviations exceed taught tolerances, without training or a robot model.
p6OGa5n0eQ.key_idea: Attach successful entry geometry to taught terrain transitions and enforce those conditions before executing fixed locomotion skills.
p6OGa5n0eQ.evidence: Evaluation includes a 27-minute teaching session, localization-noise tests, contact simulation under disturbances, and physical robot deployment across terrain transitions.
p6OGa5n0eQ.claimed_gains: Valid disturbed crossings rise from 24.1% to 88.6%, simulation records no falls in 180 climbs versus 9, and mean route distance after a 1.2 m displacement falls to 0.14 m versus 1.10 m without rejoining.
p6OGa5n0eQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical focus on transition-entry conditions and controlled deployment and simulation evidence.
p6OGa5n0eQ.main_concern: The distinct contribution of passage information over conventional route following, gait scheduling, and configured constraints is not clearly isolated.

iXkB8QQf6K.one_liner: Curvature and feature-objective moments characterize recipient-specific transfer and guide pooled or structured collaborative estimation.
iXkB8QQf6K.problem: Personalized federated learning lacks a clear account of which recipient statistics enable useful transfer beyond local learning.
iXkB8QQf6K.method: For least-squares heads on fixed shared features, the paper characterizes transfer using a curvature matrix and feature-objective cross-moment. Pooled and structured estimators exploit similarity across clients, with finite-time analysis connecting estimation quality to personalized optimization.
iXkB8QQf6K.key_idea: Estimate recipient-specific curvature and cross-moments collaboratively when shared structure makes them more accurate than local estimates.
iXkB8QQf6K.evidence: Finite-time theory is tested in favorable and unfavorable collaboration regimes, scarce CIFAR-feature settings, and exploratory nonlinear-head experiments.
iXkB8QQf6K.claimed_gains: Pooled estimation reduces error by 10–19% relative to the strongest non-oracle local or iterative comparator under scarce homogeneous CIFAR features, while structured estimation reports 4–21% reductions.
iXkB8QQf6K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit transfer-statistic characterization and analysis separating estimation error from client-population mismatch.
iXkB8QQf6K.main_concern: Exact characterization and guarantees rely on least-squares affine gradients, leaving nonlinear and practical estimator variants insufficiently covered.

Pi8HS3m8tx.one_liner: PACE segments student rollouts by teacher likelihood changes and calibrates local mismatch against an initial-prefix anchor.
Pi8HS3m8tx.problem: Token-level distillation discrepancies mix reasoning gaps with persistent lexical, formatting, and teacher-preference differences.
Pi8HS3m8tx.method: PACE partitions responses using teacher-NLL change points and structural boundaries, then forms segment-averaged student-to-teacher NLL ratios. Initial segments provide a trajectory-specific anchor for calibrating later segment ratios.
Pi8HS3m8tx.key_idea: Normalize segment-level student-teacher loss ratios by an early-prefix ratio to reduce persistent trajectory-wide mismatch.
Pi8HS3m8tx.evidence: Experiments cover multiple teacher-student pairs and six benchmarks, with tool-use evaluations and comparisons of segmentation rules.
Pi8HS3m8tx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the problem of noisy token-level discrepancies and empirical support for the segment-calibration approach.
Pi8HS3m8tx.main_concern: The assumption that early-prefix ratios isolate irrelevant mismatch and provide an appropriate target for later reasoning segments is insufficiently justified.

DG4TB9sXct.one_liner: Translates KV caches across heterogeneous LLM architectures using token-routed translator mixtures and trajectory-aligning context correction loss.
DG4TB9sXct.problem: Model-specific KV-cache spaces prevent heterogeneous LLMs in multi-agent and shared-context systems from reusing prefilled context states across different architectures.
DG4TB9sXct.method: Mixture-of-Translators (MoT) maps source-LLM context KV caches into a target LLM's cache space using multiple translator modules with token-level routing rather than a single global projection. A Context Correction Loss aligns the replayed target trajectory with the native target trajectory while balancing early-injection propagation error against late-injection correction-deficit error.
DG4TB9sXct.key_idea: Route source-model KV caches through token-level mixtures of translators into a target LLM's cache space while aligning replayed and native target trajectories via a Context Correction Loss.
DG4TB9sXct.evidence: Theoretical error-mode analysis and cross-architecture KV-cache translation experiments among Llama, Gemma, and Qwen families, including multi-agent cache-management evaluations.
DG4TB9sXct.claimed_gains: Achieves 57.6% average accuracy and 0.42 F1 across heterogeneous Llama, Gemma, and Qwen pairs, recovering 95.0% and 120.6% of native target performance and reaching 1.5x and 3.5x the strongest-baseline scores.
DG4TB9sXct.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cross-architecture KV-cache reuse across distinct LLM families is an important systems problem and find the error analysis and multi-family empirical results informative.
DG4TB9sXct.main_concern: MoT translates only a fraction of target layers and still requires target-side context replay—without replay-only controls or end-to-end latency analysis to isolate true cache-translation gains—while mixture routing shows limited ablation benefit over a single translator.

bQGsgyqrWe.one_liner: Weights per-cell flow-matching losses by cross-fitted responder probabilities to counter non-responder dilution in cell morphology generation.
bQGsgyqrWe.problem: Training generative flow-matching models on all imaged cells of a perturbation shrinks predicted morphological shifts by the fraction of responding cells, which no single classifier-free guidance strength can undo.
bQGsgyqrWe.method: The method trains a cross-fitted classifier comparing treated cells against same-plate control cells—holding out each cell's own well—to estimate per-cell response probabilities, and weights each treated cell's flow-matching loss by its estimated probability of responding.
bQGsgyqrWe.key_idea: Estimate each treated cell's response probability with a well-held-out plate-control classifier and weight its flow-matching training loss by that probability.
bQGsgyqrWe.evidence: Mathematical derivation of mixture-induced shrinkage, a controlled 1-in-10 responder dilution benchmark against a CellFlux-style baseline and labeled oracle, and real-data evaluations on BBBC021, RxRx1, and JUMP.
bQGsgyqrWe.claimed_gains: Recovers 83% of the perturbation effect versus 0% for a CellFlux-style model (and 89% for an oracle) on the 1-in-10 dilution benchmark, and reduces energy distance to real treated cells by 29% on BBBC021 and 49% on RxRx1.
bQGsgyqrWe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying non-responder mixture shrinkage in generative cell-morphology models is insightful and well validated by the controlled dilution benchmark.
bQGsgyqrWe.main_concern: Real-data non-responder assumptions break down when low-scoring treated cells remain distinguishable from controls, and evaluating against full treated populations yields mixed or degraded results (such as on JUMP) without comparisons to simpler reweighting heuristics.

YB3ZG2Ifpu.one_liner: Learns budget-constrained secondary-outcome subsets and treatment assignments via a pilot study to minimize observational ATE variance.
YB3ZG2Ifpu.problem: Existing experimental selection correction (ESC) methods fix secondary outcomes and treatment-assignment rules in advance, losing statistical efficiency under measurement-cost budgets.
YB3ZG2Ifpu.method: The authors characterize the oracle budget-constrained experimental design—jointly choosing secondary outcomes and treatment-assignment probabilities—that minimizes the semiparametric efficiency bound for observational primary ATE estimation, and propose EfficientESC, a two-stage pilot-plus-main-experiment procedure with an optional pilot-reuse estimator.
YB3ZG2Ifpu.key_idea: Use observational data and a randomized pilot to jointly select secondary outcomes and treatment-assignment probabilities that minimize the cost-constrained semiparametric efficiency bound for experimental selection correction.
YB3ZG2Ifpu.evidence: Asymptotic proofs of oracle-design convergence, normality, and semiparametric efficiency, paired with synthetic simulations testing design recovery, variance, and test calibration.
YB3ZG2Ifpu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly optimizing secondary-outcome selection and treatment allocation under measurement-cost constraints is a principled formulation backed by thorough asymptotic efficiency theory.
YB3ZG2Ifpu.main_concern: The method assumes every candidate secondary-outcome set satisfies strong latent-unconfoundedness identification conditions and is tested only in favorable synthetic simulations where simple fixed full-budget designs outperform EfficientESC at small sample sizes.

yJlnObHSlG.one_liner: Routes low temporal frequencies to reverse KL and high frequencies to Fisher divergence in video score distillation.
yJlnObHSlG.problem: Few-step video score distillation faces a trade-off where reverse KL preserves global semantics while attenuating motion dynamics, whereas Fisher divergence preserves dynamics while shifting semantics.
yJlnObHSlG.method: Showing that mode-selection errors concentrate in lower temporal frequencies and variance-retention errors concentrate in higher temporal frequencies, Temporal-Frequency Routed Distillation (TFRD) routes the low temporal-frequency band through reverse KL and the high band through Fisher divergence, using a gradient projector to keep band updates spectrally disjoint.
yJlnObHSlG.key_idea: Split video score distillation along temporal frequency—routing low bands through reverse KL and high bands through Fisher divergence—with a gradient projector enforcing spectrally disjoint updates.
yJlnObHSlG.evidence: Divergence sensitivity analysis on mixture and variance errors, plus 4-step distillation experiments on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B evaluated on VBench against DMD and SGMD baselines.
yJlnObHSlG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find routing reverse KL and Fisher divergences across temporal frequency bands conceptually well motivated and note clear VBench motion and quality gains on 4-step Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B.
yJlnObHSlG.main_concern: Experiments test only a single 1.3B text-to-video model without full adversarial DMD2 baselines or ablations isolating temporal-frequency routing from normalization changes and full-band objective combinations.

o9aYcHbl78.one_liner: Quadratic programming finds minimum-norm generative updates that jointly preserve directional effects of multiple active safety guidances.
o9aYcHbl78.problem: Suppressing multiple co-occurring undesired concepts in text-to-image generation fails under naive summation due to directional attenuation or under single-guidance selection that leaves co-occurring targets untreated.
o9aYcHbl78.method: QPS formulates multi-guidance aggregation at each denoising step as a quadratic program that computes the minimum-norm correction to the base update while preserving each active guidance source's directional projection. The authors also build CHC-Bench using a prompt-generation and verification pipeline that retains prompts producing all specified target concepts in one image.
o9aYcHbl78.key_idea: Solve a quadratic program for the minimum-norm update that satisfies directional projection constraints for every active safety guidance simultaneously.
o9aYcHbl78.evidence: Evaluated on the proposed CHC-Bench and conventional benchmarks across multiple safety guidance methods and text-to-image generative backbones.
o9aYcHbl78.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly suppressing co-occurring harmful concepts in a single image is a practical problem and that the quadratic-programming formulation and CHC-Bench are clean and intuitive.
o9aYcHbl78.main_concern: CHC-Bench supplies oracle per-prompt target concepts rather than running over all candidate concepts, where spurious activations could degrade QPS under its hard constraints, and step-wise geometric preservation may not guarantee semantic erasure.

pHBBso8AqL.one_liner: Prequential audio deepfake benchmark decomposes continual test-time adaptation into score-ordering discrimination versus threshold recalibration.
pHBBso8AqL.problem: Single-number accuracy evaluations in continual test-time adaptation for audio deepfake detection conflate degraded score ordering with threshold miscalibration against unseen synthesis systems.
pHBBso8AqL.method: The paper constructs a strictly prequential source-free, label-free continual test-time adaptation benchmark pairing ASVspoof 2019 LA source training with MLAAD spoofed and M-AILABS bona fide target streams, decomposing detection cost into discrimination and calibration components. It also introduces CAST, a neighborhood-based continual adaptation method.
pHBBso8AqL.key_idea: Score every utterance strictly before parameter updates and decompose detection cost into threshold-free discrimination (minDCF) and operating-point calibration loss.
pHBBso8AqL.evidence: Evaluated across five streams totaling 266,400 scored positions (including 52 sequential generators) using five prediction-driven CTTA methods, XLS-R and WavLM backbones, labeled reference updates, and frozen-detector recalibration.
pHBBso8AqL.claimed_gains: On the 52-generator stream, Tent lowers per-block minDCF by 0.010 and 0.013 on two held-out checkpoints versus 0.100–0.112 for labeled updates, while recalibrating the frozen detector removes 22–77% of calibration loss.
pHBBso8AqL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the detection-cost decomposition separating discrimination from calibration on a practical problem, supported by experiments across two backbones and multiple shift streams.
pHBBso8AqL.main_concern: Pairing bona fide and spoofed target audio from different corpora (with only four recurring M-AILABS speakers) introduces dataset and speaker shortcuts, and parameter-free direct neighborhood smoothing outperforms CAST-LN.

ig13XeveLQ.one_liner: Counterfactual key-value cache transplants across robot policy layers causally steer object motion from fixed simulated states.
ig13XeveLQ.problem: Internal activation edits in robot policies can move a robot toward a donor target without isolating whether controlled scene information rather than perturbation magnitude caused the behavior.
ig13XeveLQ.method: Counterfactual observations with shifted target locations generate donor key-value caches that replace recipient caches at selected policy layers while all rollouts execute from an identical simulated physical state. Directional cache differences are compared against four channel-sign transformations preserving layerwise perturbation norms within 2%.
ig13XeveLQ.key_idea: Transplant target-conditioned key-value caches into policies executing from identical simulated physics and test bidirectional endpoint shifts against norm-matched sign-flipped controls.
ig13XeveLQ.evidence: Tested on FastWAM and π0.5 across two manipulation tasks over 128 rollouts (117 reachable, 114 visually eligible states), plus non-target spatial comparisons, bounded two-axis pilots, and independent offline reconstruction.
ig13XeveLQ.claimed_gains: All four task-model cells meet the joint criterion for bidirectional relative endpoint effects exceeding equal-norm controls within 2% norm, achieving control-adjusted mean shifts of 51–72 mm.
ig13XeveLQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled experimental protocol that fixes simulated physics while using bidirectional swaps and equal-norm controls to separate scene-conditioned causal transfer from perturbation magnitude.
ig13XeveLQ.main_concern: The main confirmation is restricted to short-horizon single-axis post-grasp shifts where rendered target changes still alter low-level visual features, limiting broader scientific conclusions about long-horizon or abstract representations.

yCaCODHKwp.one_liner: Cross-trajectory attention-flow graphs align sampled reasoning paths by cumulative flow to reweight token-level GRPO advantages.
yCaCODHKwp.problem: Outcome rewards in language model reinforcement learning provide coarse supervision across hundreds of tokens, while existing attributions either isolate single trajectories or require shared prefixes.
yCaCODHKwp.method: FlowWeaver constructs prompt-to-answer propagation graphs within each sampled response using attention weights and aligns tokens across responses via cumulative flow as a shared coordinate. Conditioning path propagation on observed group outcomes yields token-level importance scores that reweight GRPO advantages.
yCaCODHKwp.key_idea: Connect multiple sampled reasoning trajectories at aligned cumulative attention-flow coordinates and measure outcome-conditioned group flow through each token to reweight advantages.
yCaCODHKwp.evidence: Evaluated in reinforcement learning experiments across mathematical reasoning, general benchmarks, and agentic tasks against GRPO and credit-assignment baselines.
yCaCODHKwp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that fine-grained credit assignment for outcome-supervised LLM reinforcement learning is an important bottleneck and note empirical gains over GRPO across mathematical and agentic tasks.
yCaCODHKwp.main_concern: Reviewers question how attention-based flow credit differs fundamentally from standard reward backpropagation or state-value advantages, and ask for qualitative validation of token-level credit accuracy.

tYTwlu5dLF.one_liner: Minimax randomized label selection and replacement-loss continuous optimization improve approximation guarantees for constrained non-monotone multi-label maximization.
tYTwlu5dLF.problem: Constrained non-monotone multi-label maximization with orthant submodular and r-wise monotone objectives suffers from suboptimal approximation guarantees on p-systems and matroids.
tYTwlu5dLF.method: Random-root selects item labels via a minimax randomized rule that minimizes worst-case local comparison loss per unit of expected gain on p-systems and matroids. A companion continuous optimization algorithm optimizes label distributions against label-dependent replacement losses on matroids with polynomial value-query bounds.
tYTwlu5dLF.key_idea: Minimize worst-case local label-comparison loss per unit gain via randomization, or optimize continuous label distributions against label-specific replacement losses.
tYTwlu5dLF.evidence: Supported by closed-form approximation proofs for r-wise monotone orthant-submodular functions on p-systems and matroids, polynomial value-query bounds, and synthetic campaign experiments with r > 2 and high audience overlap.
tYTwlu5dLF.claimed_gains: Random-root improves the matroid guarantee from 1/(r+1) to 1/(1+√r) for r ≥ 2, while continuous optimization attains strictly higher coefficients α_r with relative improvement approaching approximately 25.64%.
tYTwlu5dLF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the label-specific comparison and replacement-loss analyses establish nontrivial theoretical improvements in approximation guarantees across matroids, p-systems, and r-wise monotone orthant-submodular objectives.
tYTwlu5dLF.main_concern: Practical relevance and computational efficiency remain unclear given synthetic-only empirical evaluation, small numerical gains at k=2, and high accuracy-dependent query overhead in the continuous algorithm.

bbtcH0YFxp.one_liner: Schedules frozen-teacher inference on idle student GPUs without dedicated accelerators or blocking asynchronous RL updates.
bbtcH0YFxp.problem: All-failed GRPO groups lack reward signal, but adding teacher supervision to asynchronous RL either consumes student GPUs or stalls generation and updates.
bbtcH0YFxp.method: HitchRL offloads frozen-teacher weights to CPU and schedules deferred teacher inference during idle periods on existing generation and optimization GPUs. Independent queues let student updates consume ready targets without waiting for unfinished teacher work.
bbtcH0YFxp.key_idea: Exploit frozen-teacher target time invariance to defer inference into idle GPU gaps while asynchronously consuming whichever teacher targets are ready.
bbtcH0YFxp.evidence: Experiments use a 1.7B student on eight benchmarks with the same eight GPUs and include scheduler analyses and a 235B demonstration.
bbtcH0YFxp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the scheduler addresses a concrete resource constraint and that time-invariant frozen-teacher targets, bounded handoffs, and CPU offload form a practical design.
bbtcH0YFxp.main_concern: Reviewers most often find baseline comparisons insufficiently controlled, so accuracy and time-to-accuracy gains cannot be attributed specifically to the asynchronous execution system.

hfYmJeEq4b.one_liner: Generates coordinated multi-robot demonstrations using task-graph dependencies and residual corrections to a pose-reaching policy.
hfYmJeEq4b.problem: Human collection of long-horizon coordinated demonstrations is costly, while scripted synchronization introduces unnecessary robot waiting.
hfYmJeEq4b.method: Graph2Demo converts PDDL plans into per-agent subtask sequences and inter-agent dependencies. The graph supplies targets to a pretrained pose-reaching policy and subtask rewards to a residual policy that corrects object-interaction actions.
hfYmJeEq4b.key_idea: Use task-graph dependencies to coordinate independent robot execution while residual reinforcement learning corrects a shared reaching policy for interaction.
hfYmJeEq4b.evidence: Diffusion policies trained on generated demonstrations are evaluated across all 11 RoboFactory tasks with one to four robots under matched demonstration and student-training settings.
hfYmJeEq4b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating downstream visuomotor policies directly tests demonstration utility and that dependency-aware coordination with residual learning improves average success.
hfYmJeEq4b.main_concern: All reviewers note that removing the task graph also removes intermediate rewards, confounding coordination benefits with reward shaping.

frg7gjeiTt.one_liner: Grounds latent visual reasoning in spatial-semantic evidence and transitions latent states back toward vocabulary-aligned decoding.
frg7gjeiTt.problem: Latent visual reasoning trajectories can leave pretrained reasoning manifolds, collapse across inputs, and be bypassed during answer generation.
frg7gjeiTt.method: RIS trains on step-wise bounding boxes and region descriptions to anchor latent tokens spatially and semantically. A progressive attention bottleneck enforces their causal role, while language transition tokens bridge synthesized states to vocabulary-aligned decoding.
frg7gjeiTt.key_idea: Anchor latent reasoning tokens to regional visual evidence, force answer dependence through attention bottlenecks, and translate latent states through language transition tokens.
frg7gjeiTt.evidence: Experiments cover V*, HRBench4K, HRBench8K, MMVP, and BLINK, with closed-source, open-source, and latent-reasoning baselines plus latent-pathway interventions.
frg7gjeiTt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding and decoder bypassing are important latent-reasoning failure modes and that RIS coherently targets them with supervision, bottlenecks, and interventions.
frg7gjeiTt.main_concern: Reviewers find key mechanistic evidence qualitative or circular and state that empirical comparisons do not isolate individual mechanisms from related grounded-reasoning methods.

jmy4p8m78H.one_liner: Tracks risky memory residue through paired agent-memory updates to measure propagation beyond current-task outcomes.
jmy4p8m78H.problem: Safe current agent behavior can conceal contaminated persistent memory that propagates risk into later tasks and memory updates.
jmy4p8m78H.method: The MemResidue Test follows three rounds of memory evolution in Answer and Execution tracks using paired retention and removal interventions. It measures residue formation, later unsafe outcomes, retrieval persistence, and effects of generic safety prompting.
jmy4p8m78H.key_idea: Compare paired memory-evolution trajectories with newly generated risky carriers retained or removed to expose residual risk beyond the current response.
jmy4p8m78H.evidence: The study covers 18 models and 191 cases with human audits, lineage and risk-stratum checks, dose tests, evaluator rotations, and a representative general memory architecture.
jmy4p8m78H.claimed_gains: Across 18 models and 191 cases, residue averages 65.1% in Answer and 32.6% in Execution.
jmy4p8m78H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that safe current outcomes do not establish memory safety and praise the paired design, validation checks, and attention to persistent risk.
jmy4p8m78H.main_concern: Critical reviewers state that retaining the whole episode does not isolate risky semantics and that unstable LLM-judge measurements weaken causal attribution across updates.

pWiT6c9HT6.one_liner: Recovers unprotected conformal-retrieval feedback through counterfactual full-pool queries under cumulative coverage constraints.
pWiT6c9HT6.problem: Coverage protection alters semi-bandit feedback, preventing conformal retrieval from learning thresholds for discrete returned-document cost.
pWiT6c9HT6.method: When another miss would exceed the cumulative miss budget, the method returns the full candidate pool and uses the revealed document to evaluate the original proposed set. These counterfactual updates preserve the unprotected learner’s threshold trajectory while enforcing coverage.
pWiT6c9HT6.key_idea: Use budget-triggered full-pool returns to reveal whether the original set would have covered, decoupling protection from threshold-learning feedback.
pWiT6c9HT6.evidence: The paper proves per-query cumulative coverage and asymptotic optimal fixed-threshold cost under stated assumptions, with matched feedback ablations, protection-overhead measurements, and sensitivity analyses.
pWiT6c9HT6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the method cleanly separates path-wise coverage protection from threshold learning and provides solid asymptotic theory and thorough sensitivity experiments.
pWiT6c9HT6.main_concern: Reviewers consistently question the ideal assumptions of guaranteed-positive candidate pools and immediate correct-document identification, as well as the lack of finite-time rates.

Ci52zA88Hq.one_liner: Replaces uniform optimal-transport cluster capacities with estimated geometric basin capacities for long-tailed representation learning.
Ci52zA88Hq.problem: Balanced optimal-transport assignments enforce equal cluster mass, which conflicts with long-tailed data geometry and mixes distinct semantic classes in teacher relations.
Ci52zA88Hq.method: The authors analyze how capacity-geometry mismatch displaces assignments and corrupts teacher relation matrices. They propose PACI, which estimates evolving geometric basin capacities and uses them consistently in optimal-transport assignment and relation construction.
Ci52zA88Hq.key_idea: Estimates evolving geometric basin capacities and enforces them consistently in both optimal-transport cluster assignment and relational teacher construction.
Ci52zA88Hq.evidence: Supported by finite-batch theoretical analysis and experiments on long-tailed benchmarks, ImageNet-LT, and naturally imbalanced iNature500.
Ci52zA88Hq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying capacity-geometry mismatch in balanced optimal transport for long-tailed representation learning is an important problem with meaningful ablations.
Ci52zA88Hq.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons to prior imbalance-aware OT clustering methods (P^2OT, SP^2OT), unclear runtime/memory overhead, and theoretical bounds that appear true by construction.

wiV8704yXa.one_liner: Uses Evidence-Intervention-Claim and causal token interventions to separate hypergraph evidence propagation from autoregressive state readout failures.
wiV8704yXa.problem: Language models performing selective belief revision can propagate evidence updates accurately yet flip judgments due to autoregressive context sensitivity.
wiV8704yXa.method: They introduce the Evidence-Intervention-Claim (EIC) framework to intervene on evidence and track supporting and opposing coverage before and after updates in two 8B models. Using fixed-prefix, companion-evidence, and source-trajectory interventions alongside frozen probes, they isolate preceding-token readout effects from bitwise-identical graph residuals.
wiV8704yXa.key_idea: Applies crossed causal interventions and frozen probes under EIC to show preceding state tokens flip verdicts despite identical graph residuals.
wiV8704yXa.evidence: Evaluated on two 8B model families across FLDx2-formal and EntailmentBank with multi-seed Qwen runs and a prospective source-disjoint replication.
wiV8704yXa.claimed_gains: Updating intermediate hypergraph sources improves multihop revision over StaticSource by 9.01 points on FLDx2-formal and 34.34 on EntailmentBank; pairing a partial endpoint with itself drops Qwen joint accuracy from 94.94% to 11.24%, while changing the preceding token from partial to full raises second-state partial accuracy from 12.92% to 82.58%.
wiV8704yXa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled causal interventions separating preceding-token, companion-evidence, and history effects on readout.
wiV8704yXa.main_concern: Reviewers note the collapse occurs on an unseen output composition in a structured training setup across only two 8B models, and the architecture does not cleanly separate inference from readout.

0OwVrEh7sU.one_liner: Audits presentation sensitivity in diffusion language models, proves attention equivariance rigidity, and trains with Reasoning-State Masking and presentation randomization.
0OwVrEh7sU.problem: Rewriting a reasoning problem into an equivalent view alters whether diffusion and autoregressive language models solve it even when average accuracy barely changes.
0OwVrEh7sU.method: They construct exact transported-target Sudoku orbits and paired code/math evaluations to measure ANY/ALL view consistency, and prove row-major relative-score attention collapses to two or three offset classes under exact grid equivariance. For post-training, they combine Reasoning-State Masking (RSM) on conditional inputs with presentation randomization (PR) over equivalent views.
0OwVrEh7sU.key_idea: Combines Reasoning-State Masking with presentation randomization across exact transported orbits after proving relative-position attention rigidity under grid equivariance.
0OwVrEh7sU.evidence: Evaluated on four diffusion LMs, autoregressive baselines, 50M/100M/8B recipe studies, and Sudoku, maze, code, and mathematics tasks with pseudo-orbit controls.
0OwVrEh7sU.claimed_gains: Preserves mean-success interactions of 1.51 and 2.45 percentage points at 50M and 100M parameters, improves mean success by 2.10 points on matched mazes, and raises all-view correctness from 47.7% to 86.1% in an 8B run.
0OwVrEh7sU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the forced-target Sudoku-orbit benchmark, ANY/ALL consistency framing, and the serialization-rigidity theorem.
0OwVrEh7sU.main_concern: Reviewers point out that large-model single-decode ANY/ALL gaps confound presentation dependence with sampling randomness, PR novelty is standard, and RSM's added benefit over random states is small or unclear.

PjCnllEZP3.one_liner: Aligns visual evidence, claims, and answer units via optimal transport with a null source and calibrated claim-level certificates.
PjCnllEZP3.problem: Vision-language model answers often contain unsupported factual claims without recording which input evidence supports each claim.
PjCnllEZP3.method: Evidence Ledgers aligns evidence atoms, typed claims, and answer units through direct and claim-composed optimal transport routes with a null source, trained via null-weighted unlikelihood, counterfactual swap, and route-consistency losses, and emits calibrated SUPPORTED/WEAK/NULL certificates at inference.
PjCnllEZP3.key_idea: Couples direct and claim-mediated optimal transport with a null source to penalize unsupported claims and emit calibrated claim-level support verdicts.
PjCnllEZP3.evidence: Evaluations on Qwen3-VL-235B, InternVL3.5-38B, and Gemma-3-27B including HallusionBench and blinded human audits.
PjCnllEZP3.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-VL-235B, the human-audited unsupported-claim rate falls from 11.0% to 4.6% (versus 6.8-7.2% for matched-compute baselines), HallusionBench accuracy rises 3.4 points, and the strongest non-transport pipeline trails by 0.9 points.
PjCnllEZP3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that claim-level evidence attribution is valuable and commend the thorough blinded human audits, ablations, and multi-backbone replication.
PjCnllEZP3.main_concern: The coupled optimal-transport solver adds limited demonstrated gain over simpler null-weighted unlikelihood or softmax baselines, and presentation/organization is difficult to follow.

KlnPPPCCiO.one_liner: Formulates memristive-inspired frozen deep reservoirs as associative parallel scans with ridge-regression readouts for long-sequence classification.
KlnPPPCCiO.problem: Gradient-trained sequence models incur high training costs, while standard reservoir computing relies on dense sequential recurrences.
KlnPPPCCiO.method: MARS derives input-dependent recurrences from a memristive potentiation-depression model, removes dense recurrent matrices to enable associative parallel scans, stacks frozen random blocks with subtractive skip connections, and trains only a linear ridge-regression readout.
KlnPPPCCiO.key_idea: Replaces dense recurrent matrices with memristive-inspired input-dependent recurrences executed as associative parallel scans with frozen weights and ridge-regression readouts.
KlnPPPCCiO.evidence: Evaluations on six long-sequence time-series classification datasets against gradient-trained sequence models including Mamba and LinOSS.
KlnPPPCCiO.claimed_gains: MARS or MARS-LTF attains highest mean accuracy on two datasets and beats Mamba on five of six, training in 0.2-1.6 seconds (54-390x faster than the fastest gradient baseline, 201-13,780x faster than Mamba) with ~21x forward speedup.
KlnPPPCCiO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate connecting memristive device dynamics to parallelizable, gradient-free sequence modeling with strong speed-accuracy trade-offs.
KlnPPPCCiO.main_concern: One reviewer identified a mathematical error in Equation 13's parallel scan derivation, and the paper lacks controlled ablations isolating skip connections, depth, and parallelization.

0ZoowJF0ui.one_liner: Regenerates 88K math word problems across 12 Indic languages from executable formulas, code-computed answers, and regional Context Banks.
0ZoowJF0ui.problem: Translated Indic math benchmarks inherit Western cultural contexts, suffer from translation artifacts, and rely on saturated English sources.
0ZoowJF0ui.method: BharatMath extracts executable formulas from English problems, samples fresh operands, computes gold answers in code, and rebuilds questions around a typed Context Bank allocating culturally and regionally appropriate units and scenarios across 12 Indic languages.
0ZoowJF0ui.key_idea: Separates mathematical contracts (executable formulas with code-computed answers) from cultural framing via a typed regional Context Bank to regenerate multilingual math problems.
0ZoowJF0ui.evidence: Comprises 88,066 problems across 12 Indic languages, audited via blind cultural-plausibility ratings, LLM two-family validity audits, human checks, and evaluations of seven open-weight models.
0ZoowJF0ui.claimed_gains: Clears a cultural-plausibility criterion on 52% of items versus 0.7% for literal translation, with 82.7% of test items audited as fully valid and zero wrong golds among audit-valid items.
0ZoowJF0ui.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the core idea of decoupling executable math formulas from cultural context to avoid translation artifacts across 12 Indic languages.
0ZoowJF0ui.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about writing clarity in parts of the manuscript and the reliance on LLM judges for validity filtering (82.7% valid) without broader native-speaker human verification.

XCOAMO2G5o.one_liner: Proves calibration conditions for general Crammer-Singer surrogate losses in multi-class classification with predictor-rejector abstention.
XCOAMO2G5o.problem: The Crammer-Singer multi-class loss is not classification-calibrated to 0-1 loss when low-confidence samples have maximum class probability below 1/2.
XCOAMO2G5o.method: The authors analyze general Crammer-Singer losses composed of binary surrogates within the predictor-rejector abstention framework, where a rejector abstains on low-confidence inputs. They derive necessary and sufficient conditions for calibration by reducing multiclass conditional surrogate risk to a simpler problem in maximum class probability.
XCOAMO2G5o.key_idea: Establishes calibration conditions for general Crammer-Singer losses in predictor-rejector abstention by reducing conditional surrogate risk to maximum-class-probability optimization.
XCOAMO2G5o.evidence: Proves calibration theorems for general CS losses and reports experiments comparing ACS and MCS variants on up to 10-class datasets.
XCOAMO2G5o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the calibration problem is well-defined and the theoretical reduction and theorems for general CS losses are interesting.
XCOAMO2G5o.main_concern: Reviewers note unclear theoretical and empirical advantages over existing calibrated abstention surrogates, small/inconsistent gains with high rejection rates, and notation ambiguities.

qC88InjePl.one_liner: Quantifies the value and cost of repeated tokens in multi-epoch LLM pretraining relative to single-epoch and fresh-data runs.
qC88InjePl.problem: As pretraining increasingly repeats data, it remains unclear how many epochs to train, how optimal repeats scale with model size, and how exposure order affects loss.
qC88InjePl.method: The authors benchmark repeated tokens against two references—one epoch on the same data and fresh data at equal compute—identifying a single scaling variable (extra epochs divided by unique tokens per parameter) and a critical epoch count. They also run matched-token-count experiments varying shard replay order, repetition concentration, and source entropy.
qC88InjePl.key_idea: Prices repeated tokens against single-epoch and compute-matched fresh-data baselines, showing repetition cost scales with extra epochs per unique-token-to-parameter ratio.
qC88InjePl.evidence: Controlled multi-epoch pretraining experiments across model sizes from 127M to 2B parameters, including matched-count replay-order and source-entropy comparisons.
qC88InjePl.claimed_gains: Optimal epochs at fixed corpus fall from about 15 at 127M to 4 at 2B parameters, and replaying shards consecutively raises loss by up to 0.46 bits per byte at identical counts.
qC88InjePl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important data-reuse question and provides useful paired evidence that aggregate token counts alone do not determine loss.
qC88InjePl.main_concern: Reviewers note a scattered central narrative, unclear presentation of fixed variables and replay spacing, and single-seed or quantized evaluations at larger scales.

R5trgSDrJp.one_liner: Designs instance bags before aggregate feedback to minimize the identification width of a fixed model's AUC.
R5trgSDrJp.problem: Identical aggregate bag label means can correspond to widely varying AUC values, creating evaluation uncertainty when individual labels are unavailable.
R5trgSDrJp.method: The authors formulate bag design as minimizing the worst-case AUC interval compatible with exact population bag means, deriving an exact width formula and proving adjacent-rank grouping is optimal for distinct scores. For shared-feature repeated states, they use linear programming and width-reducing swaps.
R5trgSDrJp.key_idea: Minimizes the sharp AUC identification interval under exact aggregate bag means via adjacent-rank grouping and LP-guided swap search.
R5trgSDrJp.evidence: Theoretical proofs for sharp AUC width and optimality, plus experiments on 12-instance blocks and full-window datasets.
R5trgSDrJp.claimed_gains: Spread-out width-minimizing assignments reduce median AUC width on twelve-instance blocks (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
R5trgSDrJp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem of bag design for model evaluation rather than training novel and the mathematical AUC-width formulation clean.
R5trgSDrJp.main_concern: Reviewers note the theory assumes exact population means (failing under finite-sample or noisy counts), requires knowing model scores, and shows small gains on full-window datasets.

zqPPaYF6kt.one_liner: Meta-learns a low-rank subspace of LayerNorm updates from prior subjects to constrain unlabeled test-time adaptation.
zqPPaYF6kt.problem: Standard entropy-minimization test-time adaptation on few unlabeled medical time-series windows often degrades correct predictions.
zqPPaYF6kt.method: LSTA meta-learns a low-rank subspace of LayerNorm updates across past subjects using unlabeled support windows for entropy steps and labeled query windows to shape the subspace. At test time, adaptation is restricted to this fixed subspace using at most eight unlabeled windows.
zqPPaYF6kt.key_idea: Meta-learns a low-rank orthogonal subspace of LayerNorm updates from training subjects and projects unlabeled test-time entropy-minimization gradients onto it.
zqPPaYF6kt.evidence: Evaluated on five EEG and ECG benchmarks with subject-exclusive splits against seven TTA baselines and random-subspace controls.
zqPPaYF6kt.claimed_gains: Outperforms a random subspace in 22 of 25 dataset-seed pairs, with per-subject labeled LayerNorm updates occupying 1.2 to 1.8 effective directions.
zqPPaYF6kt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical relevance of safe few-window personalization for medical time series and the extensive robustness checks.
zqPPaYF6kt.main_concern: Reviewers note small, statistically borderline gains over LN-TTA, unvalidated low-rank inter-subject shift assumptions, and missing comparisons to prior meta-learned gradient projection methods.

AlSOI53mIP.one_liner: Distills teacher decompositions into compact one-line equation checkpoints to accelerate reasoning without full natural-language CoT.
AlSOI53mIP.problem: Explicit chain-of-thought decoding is slow, while fully latent reasoning loses accuracy and prevents inspection of intermediate steps.
AlSOI53mIP.method: HAIR uses goal-level distillation to train a student to emit only compact one-line textual checkpoints (e.g., G1=G0*2=18) for each decomposition step, with optional latent blocks before each checkpoint.
AlSOI53mIP.key_idea: Replaces verbose natural-language reasoning with distilled one-line symbolic checkpoints, optionally preceded by latent computation blocks.
AlSOI53mIP.evidence: Evaluated on GSM8K, SVAMP, GSM-Hard, and MATH using Qwen3-1.7B across multiple seeds and ablations over latent blocks and distillation.
AlSOI53mIP.claimed_gains: On GSM8K with Qwen3-1.7B, HAIR decodes 61% fewer tokens and cuts inference latency by more than half while retaining 98.8% of explicit CoT accuracy.
AlSOI53mIP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the thorough multi-seed paired ablations, including the honest negative result that latent blocks add little beyond checkpoints.
AlSOI53mIP.main_concern: Reviewers question the fairness of single-seed external baseline comparisons (CODI, Coconut) and whether checkpoints are simply compact explicit CoT.

gI7vKdGSwz.one_liner: Correlates search-tree structure with human ratings of move brilliance in chess and creativity in Wordle.
gI7vKdGSwz.problem: What computational properties of a problem-solving search space drive human perceptions of creativity remains poorly quantified.
gI7vKdGSwz.method: Analyzes expert-annotated Chess Informant games (controlling for engine evaluation and forcing moves) and a new dataset of human Wordle reactions to test whether search-tree shape predicts perceived brilliance or creativity.
gI7vKdGSwz.key_idea: Uses game-tree shape features derived from search engines to predict human annotations of brilliant chess moves and creative Wordle plays.
gI7vKdGSwz.evidence: Statistical analyses on Chess Informant (5,278 brilliant, 8,591 good, 6,192 unlabeled moves) and 173 positive Wordle examples.
gI7vKdGSwz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the research question interesting and value the expert-labeled Chess Informant dataset.
gI7vKdGSwz.main_concern: Reviewers cite weak Wordle evidence (173 positives, p = 0.047), potential conflation of forcing tactics/problem difficulty with creativity, and reliance on engine rather than human search trees.

HfrEezynfj.one_liner: Scales embedding-noise variance proportionally to the learning rate during LLM supervised fine-tuning to eliminate late-stage gradient bias.
HfrEezynfj.problem: Fixed-scale embedding noise (like NEFTune) helps early SFT generalization but leaves a non-vanishing gradient bias as the learning rate decays.
HfrEezynfj.method: AdaNoiseSFT sets the variance of random token-embedding noise proportional to the current learning rate, decaying noise to zero alongside the LR schedule without extra forward passes or optimizer state.
HfrEezynfj.key_idea: Couples embedding-noise variance directly to the instantaneous learning rate so regularization vanishes as optimization converges.
HfrEezynfj.evidence: Supported by Adam smoothing-bias analysis and multi-seed instruction-tuning experiments across cosine, linear, step, and WSD LR schedules.
HfrEezynfj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, zero-overhead, and backed by thorough ablations across learning-rate schedules.
HfrEezynfj.main_concern: Decaying injected noise is a well-known practice, and most gains come from decaying noise rather than exact LR-matching, with modest improvements over tuned linear-taper baselines.

EOyudF7xKU.one_liner: Evaluating actionability, diagnosis, and response separately reveals when CI maintenance agents patch failures they should leave alone.
EOyudF7xKU.problem: Repair benchmarks beginning with known patch tasks do not test whether agents should edit a repository, act otherwise, or defer after CI failure.
EOyudF7xKU.method: ActCI-Bench links 1,543 real failure episodes to actionability, root-cause, and response targets using logs, repository context, CI history, and developer handling. It scores classification and false repairs, including a diagnosis-before-response workflow.
EOyudF7xKU.key_idea: Selective-decision evaluation measures restraint on non-actionable failures alongside diagnosis and repair rather than assuming every episode needs a patch.
EOyudF7xKU.evidence: The benchmark contains 1,543 real episodes, including 509 non-actionable cases, with repository-disjoint splits and retrospective evidence-rich context settings.
EOyudF7xKU.claimed_gains: Repository-aware agents achieve higher macro-F1 than specialized triage baselines but still propose patches on 41-48% of non-actionable cases.
EOyudF7xKU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating appropriate intervention from patch success addresses an important and interpretable coding-agent evaluation gap.
EOyudF7xKU.main_concern: Reviewers question whether retrospective context and source-label shortcuts make the measured decisions representative of failure-time CI maintenance.

cKOn9r9ZoI.one_liner: Calibrates LLM persona generators from behavioral choice discrepancies via anchored preference adjustments and structured economic search.
cKOn9r9ZoI.problem: Plausible LLM persona prompts do not specify consistent choice behavior across models, and fitting observed choices without rich interventions can worsen counterfactual predictions.
cKOn9r9ZoI.method: Economically-Informed Persona Generators (EIPG) calibrates persona generators from simulated-versus-observed behavioral discrepancies using an anchored parameterization that preserves authored prompts while exposing sparse preference adjustments. It compares structured economic search against LLM- and text-evolution search under controlled and public discrete-choice interventions.
cKOn9r9ZoI.key_idea: Treats LLM persona grounding as an identification problem, applying sparse anchored preference adjustments calibrated from multi-intervention choice discrepancies.
cKOn9r9ZoI.evidence: Evaluated on a controlled discrete-choice benchmark, four local LLMs across three families, and public human discrete-choice data.
cKOn9r9ZoI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear demonstration that calibrating to observed choices can degrade unseen counterfactuals when intervention coverage is weak.
cKOn9r9ZoI.main_concern: Construction of target choice moments for the LLM experiments is unclear, human-data validation only tests numerical profiles where direct human estimation far outperforms EIPG (0.0758 vs 0.4491 error), and broader intervention gains are inconsistent.

SFsylGwgkZ.one_liner: Decomposes weighted-network rewiring null statistics into wiring and weight-placement terms with an exact finite-sample placement test.
SFsylGwgkZ.problem: Standard rewiring null models simultaneously alter connection topology and weight assignments, confounding structural topology effects with weight placement.
SFsylGwgkZ.method: The authors apply the null model's weight rule to both the observed topology and rewired topologies to decompose the rewiring statistic into separate wiring and weight-placement components. They also derive an exact finite-sample permutation test for placement and separate placement variance from rewiring variance.
SFsylGwgkZ.key_idea: Evaluates the null weight rule on the observed graph itself to isolate weight-placement mean and variance from topological rewiring effects.
SFsylGwgkZ.evidence: Mathematical derivations and finite-sample tests evaluated on iterative magnitude pruning of LeNet-300-100 at 95%+ sparsity (plus ResNet-20) and five connectome reservoirs.
SFsylGwgkZ.claimed_gains: Placement is statistically significant for every seed tested in LeNet-300-100 at 95% sparsity and above, and accounts for most null variance in connectome reservoirs.
SFsylGwgkZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies an important confounding factor in rewiring nulls with a clean, interpretable, distribution-free decomposition.
SFsylGwgkZ.main_concern: The mathematical decomposition is simple with qualitative overlap with prior pruning-mask shuffling work, experimental scope is small, and core notation and matched-draw definitions need clearer presentation.

vLIWSGciWk.one_liner: Monitors MoE VLA expert-routing recurrence with conformal calibration to detect execution stalls and trigger recovery primitives.
vLIWSGciWk.problem: Frozen vision-language-action policies continue executing actions after task progress has stalled, lacking a lightweight way to detect failure and recover.
vLIWSGciWk.method: NAR monitors the expert-routing trace already produced by a frozen MoE VLA, measuring recurrence relative to episode start and scoring deviations from successful source runs via nearest-neighbor distance, temporal smoothing, and episode-level conformal calibration. Triggered alarms execute a fixed release-and-lift recovery primitive before returning control to the policy.
vLIWSGciWk.key_idea: Reuses zero-marginal-cost MoE expert-routing recurrence with episode-level conformal calibration to trigger a fixed release-and-lift recovery primitive.
vLIWSGciWk.evidence: Evaluated on HiMoE-VLA across LIBERO suites (including 4,320 cross-suite episodes and 1,608 paired replay alarms) and CALVIN, plus timing studies.
vLIWSGciWk.claimed_gains: Detects 97.2% of cross-suite failures at a 1.32% episode-level false-alarm rate; paired replay of 1,608 alarms yields 175 net additional successes (10.88 percentage points per alarm, 0.40 points corpus-normalized).
vLIWSGciWk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise using existing MoE routing traces as a zero-extra-forward-pass, low-overhead (3.14 ms) monitoring signal and evaluating net rescue versus disruption.
vLIWSGciWk.main_concern: The work omits direct comparison to closest prior work VLA-FAIL, lacks real-robot validation, relies on a fixed reset-like recovery primitive, and applies only to uncommon MoE VLA architectures.

WoUjYfGYV5.one_liner: Trains a VLM reranker to jointly output relevance scores, contextual crop boxes, and answer sentences in one call.
WoUjYfGYV5.problem: Multimodal RAG pipelines feed full page images to generators, inflating token counts, while existing context pruners only handle text.
WoUjYfGYV5.method: MMProvence trains a VLM reranker (2B, 4B, and 9B) to emit a relevance score, a contextual bounding box covering supporting elements like headers or legends, and evidence sentences in a single pass per query-page pair. Surviving pages are cropped and text-pruned using these outputs without an extra pruning model call.
WoUjYfGYV5.key_idea: Folds contextual image-box cropping and sentence selection into the VLM reranker's single forward pass alongside relevance scoring.
WoUjYfGYV5.evidence: Evaluated on the eight domains of ViDoRe V3 across 2B, 4B, and 9B parameter scales with box-type ablations.
WoUjYfGYV5.claimed_gains: MMProvence-2B cuts generator input by 75% (21.6k to 5.3k tokens) with LLM-as-a-judge score 0.803 vs 0.827 full context and nDCG@10 0.601 vs 0.604; contextual boxes drop score by 2.7 points vs 13.3 for tight boxes; 4B/9B reach nDCG@10 0.627/0.636 with 9B scoring 0.822.
WoUjYfGYV5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical single-pass reranking-and-pruning design, strong token reduction on ViDoRe V3, and the insight that contextual bounding boxes preserve answer quality.
WoUjYfGYV5.main_concern: The zero-cost claim ignores extra reranker output tokens and cost-matched baselines, box ablations are confounded by box size, the same model acts as generator and judge, and RegionRAG is missing.

a4AhDiAVL0.one_liner: Shows mid-conversation persona-vector shifts reflect context contamination and steers along composite frozen persona, coherence, and repetition directions.
a4AhDiAVL0.problem: Re-extracting LLM persona directions mid-conversation yields rotated, shrunk vectors that prior work misinterprets as representation drift, while strong persona steering degrades coherence and induces repetition.
a4AhDiAVL0.method: The authors show that mid-conversation direction shrinkage tracks added conversational content rather than persona identity, validating the pre-conversation frozen direction for monitoring and closed-loop steering. They additionally extract coherence and repetition directions and steer along a weighted composite of all three vectors.
a4AhDiAVL0.key_idea: Monitors and steers along the frozen pre-conversation persona direction combined with coherence and repetition steering vectors.
a4AhDiAVL0.evidence: Evaluated on multi-turn unsteered and steered conversations, including 72 held-out conversations judged by an LLM-as-a-judge.
a4AhDiAVL0.claimed_gains: Closed-loop steering along the frozen direction raises judged persona adherence to 86 versus 11 without steering on the primary model.
a4AhDiAVL0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the mechanistic distinction between frozen and re-extracted persona directions and the controlled length-matched test revealing context contamination.
a4AhDiAVL0.main_concern: Experiments do not rule out genuine persona-representation change or content-persona correlation, and composite steering shows unclear gains over simply lowering persona-only steering strength.

uR3pznHoyG.one_liner: Routes token-level distillation feedback from frozen perception and reasoning experts using image-perturbation sensitivity and entropy inside multimodal RLVR.
uR3pznHoyG.problem: Shared outcome-level rewards in multimodal RLVR cannot distinguish visual perception errors from reasoning errors occurring within the same generated response.
uR3pznHoyG.method: RLRD uses image-perturbation sensitivity and predictive entropy as routing proxies to select which on-policy response tokens receive feedback from frozen perception or reasoning expert models. The routed teacher-student log-probability gaps are fed into a sign-preserving advantage reweighting rule that adjusts local update magnitudes while keeping the verifier's update direction.
uR3pznHoyG.key_idea: Uses image-perturbation sensitivity and token entropy to route token-level log-probability feedback from frozen perception and reasoning teachers into sign-preserving RLVR advantage reweighting.
uR3pznHoyG.evidence: Evaluated on six vision-language benchmarks with Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 7B students, including random-routing, swapped-expert, and averaged-expert ablations.
uR3pznHoyG.claimed_gains: Improves over the strongest non-RLRD baseline in each group by 1.39–2.02 percentage points across six vision-language benchmarks.
uR3pznHoyG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating perception and reasoning feedback in multimodal RLVR is well motivated and yields consistent gains across two model scales and six benchmarks.
uR3pznHoyG.main_concern: Reviewers view the method as an incremental, complex combination of existing techniques (RLSD, VPPO, H-OPD) that relies on strong assumptions of having pretrained specialist experts and lacks compute overhead analysis.

INHDdJM6sY.one_liner: Coordinates fair federated learning via a server-side price controller on global fairness residuals and a closed-form local sample-reweighting rule.
INHDdJM6sY.problem: Guaranteeing global group fairness in federated learning is difficult because fairness is measured on the pooled population while clients optimize over heterogeneous private local datasets.
INHDdJM6sY.method: GloReFair separates global fairness monitoring from local emphasis allocation: a server-side controller updates channel prices from global fairness residuals, and clients compute per-sample training weights via a unique closed-form rule derived from the Lagrangian of a round-wise allocation problem. The paper also proves single-step centralized equivalence and controller expressivity.
INHDdJM6sY.key_idea: Server-side dual prices updated from global fairness residuals drive a closed-form Lagrangian sample-reweighting rule on each heterogeneous client.
INHDdJM6sY.evidence: Supported by single-step centralized equivalence and expressivity theorems, plus experiments on three federated benchmarks across EO/EOD, three heterogeneity types, five severity levels, and eight baselines.
INHDdJM6sY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating global fairness feedback from closed-form local sample reweighting is clean and extensively tested under diverse heterogeneity regimes.
INHDdJM6sY.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over FedFB's channel-level reweighting, lack of end-to-end fairness convergence guarantees for the coupled multi-step algorithm, and strong assumptions (binary tasks, full participation, exact pooled statistics).

hGwizbsmEG.one_liner: Audits when held-out log-score gains certify new conditional information by combining baseline approximation-error bounds with finite-sample uncertainty.
hGwizbsmEG.problem: A model achieving higher held-out predictive log-score may simply exploit existing information better rather than using genuinely new conditional information.
hGwizbsmEG.method: The paper derives an exact reverse-to-forward KL conversion for a known categorical baseline using its minimum probability and a single scalar root, and constructs a failure-aware witness for sampled reports via simultaneous probability intervals and normalization constraints. Combining these baseline approximation bounds with finite-sample uncertainty certifies when predictive gains imply positive conditional mutual information.
hGwizbsmEG.key_idea: Combines an exact scalar-root reverse-to-forward KL conversion and simultaneous probability intervals with finite-sample bounds to certify conditional information from log-score gains.
hGwizbsmEG.evidence: Supported by proofs, controlled 100-class and 3-class audits, a one-coefficient Bayesian example, and analyses on WDBC, Digits, and Wine datasets.
hGwizbsmEG.claimed_gains: In a 100-class controlled audit, gives 300/300 positive certificates vs 7/300 for a generic bound; in a 3-class sampled setting, gives 91/100 positives vs 25/100 (exact envelope) and 3/100 (generic envelope); certifies 6 of 9 analyses on WDBC, Digits, and Wine.
hGwizbsmEG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formally distinguishing predictive improvement from new conditional information is valuable and that the fixed-reference categorical conversion is mathematically clean.
hGwizbsmEG.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the method's practical bottleneck remains unresolved because obtaining a sufficiently tight baseline approximation-error bound is infeasible for intractable high-dimensional baselines.

nFTFKpz3LX.one_liner: Decomposes Gradient Origin Networks to show one-step inference requires training reconstruction through the decoder's own gradient map.
nFTFKpz3LX.problem: Autoencoder decoders that reconstruct well under direct latent optimization perform poorly under Gradient Origin Networks' one-step gradient inference, and it is unclear what decoder property enables one-step inference.
nFTFKpz3LX.method: The authors separate reconstruction capacity from inference quality across linear and nonlinear decoders, proving linear one-step inference requires an isotropic decoder Gram matrix. Through controlled interventions on pretrained autoencoders, they test Jacobian conditioning, post-hoc linear code maps, and training through the decoder's inference gradient.
nFTFKpz3LX.key_idea: Demonstrates via linear Gram-matrix analysis and nonlinear interventions that one-step inference succeeds not from Jacobian conditioning alone, but by training reconstruction through the decoder's own local gradient map.
nFTFKpz3LX.evidence: Provides exact linear analysis and nonlinear diagnostic experiments on image reconstruction comparing GONs and untied autoencoders with step-size, origin, frozen-code, and decoder-transfer controls.
nFTFKpz3LX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well organized and that the capacity-versus-inference decomposition and single-hypothesis interventions provide a clean diagnostic of GONs.
nFTFKpz3LX.main_concern: Reviewers view the main finding as somewhat expected while leaving open how gradient descent finds suitable nonlinear decoders, note unclear practical significance, and spot a mathematical inconsistency in Table 1's geometric statistics.
