DHZ7ZFaFZ6.one_liner: Adapts contrastive RL to PDDL symbolic planning via a two-level policy that selects and solves one goal atom at a time.
DHZ7ZFaFZ6.problem: Vanilla contrastive reinforcement learning fails on PDDL symbolic planning because training a policy to reach a full conjunctive goal state causes the critic to ignore individual action advantages.
DHZ7ZFaFZ6.method: The authors decompose symbolic planning into two model-free policies trained with contrastive RL: a high-level policy that selects the next goal atom to pursue and a low-level policy that achieves a single goal atom, solving tasks sequentially atom by atom.
DHZ7ZFaFZ6.key_idea: Replaces full-goal contrastive RL with a hierarchical two-policy scheme where a high-level policy picks one goal atom at a time for a low-level contrastive policy to achieve.
DHZ7ZFaFZ6.evidence: Provides theoretical analysis of vanilla CRL failure and empirical evaluations on PDDL symbolic planning benchmarks.
DHZ7ZFaFZ6.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers note the under-explored model-free RL framing for symbolic planning and find the motivating analysis easy to follow, though one reviewer lists no strengths.
DHZ7ZFaFZ6.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the restrictive assumption that goals are arbitrarily serializable atom by atom, missing literature review (e.g., ConPoLe and RL planning heuristics), and unsupported or confusing claims.

j8GSV186VS.one_liner: Models coupled self-improvement loops via path decomposition and shared correction budgets to predict joint recursive self-deterioration.
j8GSV186VS.problem: Self-improving AI systems combine multiple feedback loops that are ablated individually, missing cross-mechanism couplings that can trigger recursive self-deterioration even when each loop improves alone.
j8GSV186VS.method: The authors model each self-training round as the coupled evolution of learner, inherited defect, and environment, using path decomposition to isolate cross-mechanism routes missed by leave-one-out ablations. They derive exact stability boundaries for linear recursions and show how quadratic protected readouts can deteriorate jointly while internal evaluations appear stable.
j8GSV186VS.key_idea: Uses Jacobian path decomposition and a shared learner correction budget to characterize cross-mechanism feedback routes that shift coupled self-training from improvement to recursive self-deterioration.
j8GSV186VS.evidence: Provides theoretical path-decomposition and linear/quadratic boundary results alongside small-scale nonlinear digit-classification self-training experiments.
j8GSV186VS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that analyzing how individually benign self-improvement loops can couple into instability via path decomposition and shared correction budgets addresses an important problem.
j8GSV186VS.main_concern: Reviewers note that the nonlinear digit experiments do not cleanly validate the linear instability predictions, factorial ablations diverge from single-trajectory theory, writing is overly abstract, and novelty over control theory is modest.

XADrkO76DT.one_liner: Trains a self-evolving alpha-factor mining LLM agent with hierarchical process-reward RL and failure-diagnosed experience reuse.
XADrkO76DT.problem: Prompt-based and one-shot LLM alpha-factor miners cannot continuously improve from noisy financial feedback or attribute which revision steps improved out-of-sample stability.
XADrkO76DT.method: EvoMind runs a closed hypothesize-implement-backtest-reflect loop trained with hierarchical gated process rewards scoring executability, diversity, predictive power, and hidden-window stability at every turn. It also stores diagnosed outcomes from both successful and failed trajectories in an experience bank to guide future revisions.
XADrkO76DT.key_idea: Trains a closed-loop alpha-mining agent with gated turn-level hierarchical process rewards (including hidden-window stability) and an experience bank diagnosing both successes and failures.
XADrkO76DT.evidence: Evaluated across multiple financial markets and out-of-sample settings using a Qwen3-4B backbone over five seeds with trajectory-reward and experience-retrieval ablations.
XADrkO76DT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the end-to-end RL infrastructure, gated turn-level reward hierarchy, and controlled trajectory-level and experience-bank ablations are well aligned with factor discovery.
XADrkO76DT.main_concern: Reviewers note all experiments use a single small 4B backbone (handicapping frontier-model baselines re-implemented on 4B), modest effect sizes, and an ablation that does not cleanly isolate hidden-window visibility from cross-period supervision.

CdxFd9WDU6.one_liner: Diagnoses where and how predictive world models store memory using nested causal interventions and directional Lyapunov factors.
CdxFd9WDU6.problem: Linear probing shows what information a world model encodes but cannot distinguish mechanistically incompatible memory implementations across stateless and recurrent architectures.
CdxFd9WDU6.method: The authors introduce nested interventional diagnostics: stable retention (SR) over latent rollouts, a 2x2 interventional causal separation test toggling recurrent hidden state, and a causal-subspace Lyapunov factor lambda_v(t). They apply these tools to stateless JEPA, GRU, and LSTM world models and test encoder-geometry rotations in MiniHack.
CdxFd9WDU6.key_idea: Replaces correlational probing with rollout stable retention, a 2x2 hidden-state toggle intervention, and directional Lyapunov factors to locate memory and quantify selective subspace preservation.
CdxFd9WDU6.evidence: Evaluated on delayed working-memory tasks and MiniHack across stateless JEPA, GRU, and LSTM models trained over multiple seeds, including orientation-matched encoder rotation controls.
CdxFd9WDU6.claimed_gains: JEPA, GRU, and LSTM all reach 1.000 probe accuracy while differing mechanistically; at horizon K = 5, stateless JEPA contracts average latent distances (kappa ~ 0.36) while amplifying the causal direction 6.48x relative to a typical direction.
CdxFd9WDU6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that demonstrating identical linear-probe accuracy hides incompatible memory mechanisms—and validating encoder geometry via controlled rotation in MiniHack—is compelling.
CdxFd9WDU6.main_concern: Reviewers note that trajectory-distance retention is not linked to downstream control decisions, seed-dependent solution diversity and line-attractor selective preservation overlap prior RNN literature, and the causal separation test may hold by construction.

ucbT85W9sr.one_liner: Discovers selective pseudo-groups via Gaussian noise perturbation stability, applies reliability-weighted debiasing, and corrects residual shortcuts at inference.
ucbT85W9sr.problem: Unsupervised debiasing methods that assign binary pseudo-groups from single unperturbed representations fail under weak bias or ambiguous samples.
ucbT85W9sr.method: The framework applies Gaussian Noise Intervention (GNI) to test intra-class geometric distance stability across local perturbations, partitions each class into pseudo-aligned, pseudo-conflicting, and uncertain sets with multi-view reliability weights, and adds inference-time residual-shortcut correction.
ucbT85W9sr.key_idea: Perturb representations with local Gaussian noise to measure geometric stability, selectively partition samples into aligned/conflicting/uncertain pseudo-groups, and apply reliability-weighted training plus inference correction.
ucbT85W9sr.evidence: Evaluated without group labels across four benchmarks (including medical datasets MIMIC-CXR+NIH and GbP) over multiple bias ratios and five seeds.
ucbT85W9sr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the strict annotation-free setting and multi-ratio medical benchmark evaluations showing strong worst-group accuracy.
ucbT85W9sr.main_concern: Reviewers question whether GNI adds information over deterministic clean distances since the noise preserves the clean statistic in expectation, and note missing clean-score baselines and narrow ablations.
